meta.name: e2_commitment_rig
meta.design: FCIM held FIXED (golden v5 subset, 19 rows / 69 conditions, 12 functions) + golden SDD; FHA is the only variable; pairs exact by condition id
meta.v3AddText:
COMMITMENT TEST — apply this to the severity field BEFORE you leave it empty. Table A6 rows discriminate on exactly two things: WHAT is degraded, injured or lost, and HOW MUCH. The test is therefore mechanical, not a matter of how confident you feel: read back the effects YOU just wrote for the worst applicable phase. If those effects name both the what and the degree, a Table A6 row already fits them — commit that class and cite its anchor. Withholding a class your own stated effects support is not caution, it is work left undone.
BORDERLINE IS NOT A REASON TO ABSTAIN. A condition sitting between two classes means you HAVE the facts and are weighing them, which is the ordinary case in an FHA and not a grounding failure. Commit the class your stated effects support, cite that anchor, and name the competing class in the rationale so the engineer can see the call you made and overturn it in seconds. An empty severity where you actually held a view is the single outcome this rule exists to prevent.
IF YOU DO ABSTAIN, NAME WHAT IS MISSING. Leave severity and sevBasis empty and begin the rationale with 'SEVERITY WITHHELD - need: ' followed by the SPECIFIC missing fact — a detection means, an exposure time, an occupant count, a performance margin, the phase in which it applies. If you cannot name one, you are not abstaining, you are omitting: go back and apply the test above.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric forward thrust across the aircraft (malfunction)
rows.effAc: Yawing/rolling moment about the CG; at the 28 m outboard moment arm this is the directional-control sizing case. Requires rudder authority to hold heading; at/after V1 during take-off the transient reduces controllability margin.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload to counter asymmetry with rudder and to identify/manage the affected engine.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects (asymmetric moment, reduced directional-control margin at the outboard moment arm) are grounded, but the magnitude spread — a single-engine asymmetry the rudder is sized to hold vs. a larger asymmetry — spans more than one class. The FHA must split by degree/phase before a class is derived; severity left empty pending that split and the controllability substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous forward thrust not matching commanded setting (malfunction)
rows.effAc: Delivered thrust differs from crew/autothrottle command; departs intended speed/energy state. If symmetric, an energy-management error; if it drives one engine differently, becomes an asymmetry case.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect the mismatch against thrust indication and revert to manual thrust management.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This condition is not present in the connected FCIM (SF-001 rows carry TL/PL/M only) so it lacks a modelled definition to bound the amount/direction of the error. Without the erroneous-thrust bound (single engine vs. all engines, high vs. low) the aircraft effect cannot be pinned to one class. Add the FCIM entry, then classify.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced available forward thrust (partial loss)
rows.effAc: Reduced thrust reduces climb gradient and available performance; four-engine aircraft designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following loss of any one engine at/after V1. Degree of reduction determines margin loss.
rows.effCrew: Crew manage reduced-performance profile and, if an engine is involved, execute engine-out procedures.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD substantiates continued flight after loss of one engine, but 'reduced available forward thrust' spans a benign partial reduction through to loss approaching the one-engine-out case; the amount of impairment is not fixed by the function definition, so the class is not yet derivable. Split by degree (within continued-flight margin vs. beyond) then classify.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of forward thrust generation (total loss, all engines)
rows.effAc: Total loss of propulsive thrust from all four engines. Aircraft cannot sustain flight; forced descent with no thrust available to arrest it. The dispatch case substantiates continuation after one engine only; loss of all thrust is outside that case.
rows.effCrew: Crew face a total loss-of-thrust emergency with no engine-out reconfiguration available.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers on board.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of forward thrust generation removes the aircraft's ability to sustain flight, leading to a forced descent that cannot be arrested and loss of the airplane. Effects support the Catastrophic anchor. PROPOSED for engineer confirmation; probability objective (Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh) is owned by the quantitative assessment. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded reverse thrust deployment (malfunction)
rows.effAc: Reversers fitted to the two inboard engines only; deployment inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical sleeve lock. An uncommanded in-flight deployment produces asymmetric drag/thrust reversal (inboard moment arm) with a large loss of performance and controllability; on the ground it is the intended function.
rows.effCrew: In flight, crew must counter the asymmetry and manage the affected engine; the multiple independent inhibits (WOW + RA + mechanical lock) bear on how the condition arises.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects (asymmetric drag at the inboard moment arm, performance/controllability loss in flight) are grounded, but the in-flight case is guarded by three independent inhibits and the ground case is the normal function — so the condition must be split by phase (in-flight uncommanded vs. ground) before a class is derived. Severity left empty pending that phase split and the controllability substantiation for an in-flight deployment.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on the ground (reverse developed on one inboard engine, not the other, or unequal between the two inboard reversers)
rows.effAc: Yawing moment during the ground roll biased to one side; reversers are on the two inboard engines only (~0.18 semi-span), so the asymmetric moment arm is smaller than the outboard directional sizing case. Directional control is by nose-wheel steering and rudder; deceleration is dominated by wheel braking with reverse supplemental.
rows.effCrew: Crew detect the yaw and asymmetry discrete; corrective steering/rudder and, if required, stow of reverse — increased workload during a high-tempo ground phase on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only. No occupants beyond crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is a controllable-vs-uncontrollable question on the ground: whether the asymmetric inboard reverser yaw can be countered by steering/rudder within the available runway and lateral margin is a directional-control and stopping-distance determination not supported by the SDD (no reverser thrust value, no lateral excursion margin, no steering/rudder authority-vs-asymmetry data). Cannot derive class without that; leaving blank rather than guessing.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust developing below the detection threshold (crew unaware; no annunciation, crew continue normal ground roll)
rows.effAc: A yawing moment develops on the ground below the level that alerts the crew; with reversers on the two inboard engines the asymmetric arm is inboard. Because it is below detection, no corrective reverser stow is commanded and the yaw is countered, if at all, only by the crew's routine steering/rudder inputs.
rows.effCrew: Crew unaware of the source and take no specific action regarding it; they fly/steer the ground roll normally, which routinely worsens the outcome relative to the aware case.
rows.effPax: Flight crew only; hold unoccupied in flight.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Same governing determination as SF-002-M2 (directional controllability and stopping distance on a semi-prepared strip), made worse by the unaware assumption. The SDD gives no reverser thrust magnitude, no below-threshold asymmetry level, and no lateral-excursion margin, so the aircraft-level effect (runway/lateral excursion vs controllable deviation) cannot be derived. Severity left blank per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced ground reverse thrust (reverse available but at diminished effectiveness on both inboard engines)
rows.effAc: Less supplemental deceleration from reverse; stopping relies more heavily on wheel braking (SF-008). Reverse is supplemental to the braking/flotation design; the operating margin is the 1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout at max landing weight.
rows.effCrew: Crew apply braking to compensate; potential increased braking effort/attention. No loss of directional control implied (symmetric reduction).
rows.effPax: Flight crew only; hold unoccupied in flight.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Whether reduced (symmetric) reverse consumes the stopping margin depends on the reverse contribution to the deceleration budget on a semi-prepared surface — a number the SDD does not give (it states the margin rests on braking and flotation, with reverse supplemental). Without the reverse share of the deceleration budget the reduction in safety margin cannot be sized, so class cannot be derived. Left blank.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground reverse thrust (no reverse available on either inboard engine)
rows.effAc: Deceleration on the ground is by wheel braking and flotation alone; reverse contributes nothing. The braking/flotation design carries the 1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout, with brake accumulator sized to six full applications with all three hydraulic systems lost.
rows.effCrew: Crew stop on wheel braking with reverse unavailable; potential increased braking demand and attention on a semi-prepared strip.
rows.effPax: Flight crew only; hold unoccupied in flight.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states the stopping margin rests on braking and flotation with reverse supplemental, but does not quantify reverse's contribution to the certified stopping distance. If reverse is not credited in the demonstrated landing distance, total loss may be Minor/No Safety Effect; if it is credited, loss consumes margin and could be Major. This is a performance/margin determination not derivable from the SDD, so severity is left blank rather than reaching for the benign end.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command (aircraft rolls in a manner different from that commanded — wrong direction, wrong magnitude, or uncommanded roll following a command)
rows.effAc: Aircraft departs the commanded roll attitude; on a 160 m span high-wing freighter carrying a 105 m/72.6 t single blade, an erroneous roll can produce a bank/attitude excursion that, if unarrested, leads to loss of control of aircraft trajectory. Roll is by two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers under three dissimilar flight control computers.
rows.effCrew: Crew must recognise the erroneous response, potentially against envelope-protection/degraded-law annunciation, and counter it; a hard-over or wrong-sense roll at low altitude imposes high workload with limited time to recover.
rows.effPax: Flight crew only; hold unoccupied in flight. No occupants beyond crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An erroneous (wrong-sense or hard-over) roll response is a malfunction of the roll axis of Control aircraft trajectory; at low altitude on approach/take-off an uncorrected roll excursion leads to loss of control and loss of the aeroplane. Effects support the Catastrophic anchor. This is a PROPOSED class for confirmation; the magnitude/rate of the erroneous response (hard-over vs limited-authority) is not given and would refine it. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded roll motion with no crew or autopilot command
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD describes roll actuation (two-segment ailerons, multi-function spoilers, each aileron on two hydraulic systems) but does not state the aircraft-level effect of an uncommanded roll excursion (loss of safety margin, controllability, or occupant injury). Cannot derive severity without the roll-axis controllability/handling-qualities consequence; flight phases also not determinable from the SDD.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded roll divergence developing below the detection threshold
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The 'below detection threshold' qualifier is a detectability/crew-awareness property; the SDD does not state the aircraft effect of an undetected slow roll divergence, so no effect can be assigned to any flight phase and severity cannot be derived. Missing input: roll-axis controllability effect and detection/annunciation behaviour.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded roll authority remaining within manoeuvre limits
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — 'Within manoeuvre limits' implies retained capability, but the SDD does not characterise the residual roll margin or its effect on the aircraft, crew workload, or occupants. Without a stated effect the class cannot be derived and must not be defaulted to a benign value. Missing input: quantified roll-axis safety/handling margin for the degraded case.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded roll authority outside manoeuvre limits
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD does not state the aircraft-level effect of roll authority falling outside manoeuvre limits (reduction in safety margins, controllability at the sizing case, or occupant consequence), so severity cannot be derived. Missing input: roll-axis controllability effect when authority is outside manoeuvre limits, and the applicable flight phases.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded roll authority developing below the detection threshold
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — 'Below detection threshold' is a crew-awareness/detectability property; the SDD states no aircraft effect for undetected roll-authority degradation, so no per-phase effect and no severity can be derived. Missing input: roll-axis controllability effect for the unaware case and the detection/annunciation behaviour that bounds it.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of roll control authority
rows.effAc: Aircraft cannot be manoeuvred or trimmed in roll by any means; loss of ability to maintain wings-level or to counter roll upsets, engine-out asymmetry or gusts. Loss of control of the flight path in the lateral axis.
rows.effCrew: Crew unable to arrest or control bank; no procedural recovery for total loss of roll authority.
rows.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only)
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of a primary axis of control of the aircraft trajectory prevents continued controlled flight; effects support loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to crew command
rows.effAc: Aircraft pitches in a manner not matching the crew command (wrong sense or magnitude); potential pitch excursion, exceedance of manoeuvre/structural limits or unsafe attitude, most critical in take-off/landing where recovery margin is smallest.
rows.effCrew: Crew commands are followed by an unexpected pitch response; workload and confusion in diagnosing and countering the erroneous response.
rows.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only)
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous response in the pitch axis to crew input, if in the adverse sense at low altitude, can produce an unrecoverable excursion; effects support loss of the airplane. Confirm whether magnitude bounding/envelope protection limits the worst case below Catastrophic. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch motion with no crew command
rows.effAc: Pitch surface moves without a crew command, driving an uncommanded pitch change; potential attitude/flight-path excursion and structural or manoeuvre-limit exceedance, most critical near the ground where recovery margin is smallest.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded motion, override or trim against it and diagnose the source; increased workload and startle.
rows.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only)
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded, sustained pitch input can produce a divergent excursion that, at low altitude, may be unrecoverable; effects support loss of the airplane. Confirm whether the authority/rate of any single uncommanded input is bounded and whether crew override is credited. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded pitch divergence below crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
rows.effAc: A slow uncommanded pitch/trim drift develops below the crew detection threshold; with the crew continuing normal duties and taking no action, the drift accumulates toward an attitude, speed or flight-path deviation and eventual mistrim before it is recognised.
rows.effCrew: Assumed unaware; crew take no corrective action until the deviation becomes apparent, by which point the recovery margin and available control authority may be reduced.
rows.effPax: None (hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only)
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the end state from the function definition alone: the outcome depends on the maximum trim/pitch runaway rate and end-stop authority, the deviation reached before an independent alert or symptom triggers detection, and the recovery margin remaining at that point — none of which are given at aircraft-function level. Needs the detection/annunciation and authority-bounding data (SFHA/design input) before a class can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded pitch authority outside manoeuvre limits
rows.effAc: Available pitch authority falls below that needed to command the manoeuvres the flight envelope requires; the aircraft cannot be trimmed or manoeuvred within its intended envelope, with a large reduction in longitudinal safety margins.
rows.effCrew: Crew retains partial pitch response but cannot achieve required attitude/flight-path control; excessive workload compensating, potentially reaching mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim only.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects describe a large reduction in longitudinal safety margins and excessive crew workload impairing task performance, short of loss of the aircraft given remaining partial authority and the mechanical trim reversion path; per AC 25.1309-1B this maps to Hazardous ↔ Extremely Remote 1e-7/fh. Confirm against final envelope-limit definition. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of pitch control authority
rows.effAc: No means to command pitch; the aircraft cannot control its flight path in the longitudinal axis. With all three flight control computers lost, only a survivable but degraded mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim remains; complete loss of pitch is not survivable.
rows.effCrew: Crew have no effective pitch control input; unable to arrest or command flight-path change in pitch.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of pitch control authority prevents controlled flight and would result in loss of the airplane; per AC 25.1309-1B Catastrophic ↔ Extremely Improbable 1e-9/fh. The mechanical trim reversion is a degraded partial means and does not restore full authority, so it does not downgrade the total-loss condition. Confirm. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response to crew command
rows.effAc: Yaw surface responds incorrectly to crew command (wrong sense or magnitude), producing an unintended sideslip/yaw excursion; on this four-engine high-wing airframe the directional axis is sized by the outboard-engine-out case at the 28 m moment arm, so an erroneous response near that condition risks a large reduction in directional safety margin.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect the erroneous response and counter it; workload increases and control of directional flight path is degraded until the erroneous input is isolated.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class without knowing the bounded magnitude/authority of the erroneous yaw response (full-deflection hardover vs limited excursion) — the split-rudder segmentation and per-segment authority determine whether the excursion is a large reduction in margin (Hazardous) or catastrophic near the engine-out limit. Provide the yaw-command failure-mode bound and rudder segment authority to classify.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw motion with no command
rows.effAc: Yaw develops with no crew command (uncommanded surface deflection/hardover), producing sideslip and a yaw/roll coupling the crew did not command; magnitude and its effect on directional safety margin depend on the affected rudder segment and its authority.
rows.effCrew: Crew must recognise the uncommanded motion and apply counter-input/isolate the failed segment; increased workload and degraded directional control until isolated.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class without the bounded authority of an uncommanded deflection (single-segment vs both segments, hardover vs limited) — the document gives the split-segment arrangement but not the resulting worst-case yaw excursion. With that bound an excursion could range from Major to Catastrophic depending on phase and proximity to the engine-out sizing case; provide the failure-mode authority bound to classify.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of yaw control authority
rows.effAc: No means to command yaw; aircraft cannot counter asymmetric thrust or maintain coordinated directional control. Against the directional-control sizing case (outboard engine failure at V1 with maximum blade payload at the 28 m moment arm), loss of yaw control leads to loss of directional control and departure.
rows.effCrew: Crew cannot arrest yaw excursion by any means; mechanical reversion to the lower rudder segment is a survivable but degraded path only if the loss is not total.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With the engine-out-at-V1 sizing case, complete loss of yaw control removes the ability to counter asymmetric outboard thrust, driving loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded yaw authority within manoeuvre limits
rows.effAc: Reduced yaw authority, but directional control retained within manoeuvre limits; a single rudder supply loss (segment A or B) is intended to leave sufficient authority for the engine-out sizing case.
rows.effCrew: Reduced authority may increase directional-control workload, particularly in crosswind or engine-out conditions.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states a single rudder supply loss must still leave sufficient authority for the engine-out case, but does not quantify the residual margin or workload increase for 'within limits'; effect could support Minor or Major depending on how the retained margin relates to the sizing case. Confirm the intended residual authority.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded yaw authority outside manoeuvre limits
rows.effAc: Yaw authority degraded beyond manoeuvre limits; insufficient directional control margin for the engine-out-at-V1 sizing case, giving a large reduction in directional safety margin and functional capability.
rows.effCrew: Excessive workload to maintain directional control; may be unable to hold heading against asymmetric thrust.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Yaw authority outside manoeuvre limits against the engine-out sizing case is a large reduction in safety margins / functional capabilities; short of total loss so not driven to Catastrophic. Confirm against the directional-control sizing analysis. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded yaw authority developing below detection threshold
rows.effAc: Yaw authority degrades latently below the detection threshold; the reduced margin is unannunciated and may only become apparent when directional demand (engine-out or crosswind) arrives.
rows.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action; continue duties normally until demand reveals the shortfall, at which point authority may be insufficient.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on the detection-threshold value, the rate of degradation, and the timing/magnitude of the yaw demand when it arrives — none quantified in the SDD. Cannot derive severity; not benign, so not No Safety Effect. Requires the detection-threshold and demand-coincidence data.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded yaw divergence below detection threshold
rows.effAc: Uncommanded slow yaw divergence develops below the detection threshold; aircraft departs commanded heading/sideslip without crew command, with the resulting excursion depending on divergence rate and time to detection.
rows.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action; the divergence is not annunciated and continues until it becomes perceptible or produces a secondary cue.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The divergence rate, the detection threshold, and the resulting sideslip/heading excursion and its structural or controllability consequence are not specified in the SDD; cannot derive an aircraft effect severe enough to classify. Not benign, so severity left empty rather than No Safety Effect. Requires divergence-rate and threshold data.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement with no crew command
rows.effAc: Uncommanded change of high-lift configuration alters lift, drag and pitching moment without crew command. At low speed near stall margins on take-off or approach this can produce an abrupt trajectory departure; at cruise it can overspeed a deployed surface. The upset is not part of the sizing case for the low-speed margin.
rows.effCrew: Startle and immediate high-workload recovery to arrest an uncommanded pitch/speed excursion at a phase where margins are already reduced; possible degraded-configuration landing.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction is clear (uncommanded configuration change with a trajectory upset at low-speed phases), but the SDD does not state the magnitude of the excursion, the low-speed margin available, or whether recovery is assured within the envelope. Whether this reaches Hazardous (large reduction in safety margins) or Catastrophic depends on the worst-case speed/altitude at deployment, which is not derivable from the provided definition. Leaving severity for engineering assessment.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous high-lift response to crew selection
rows.effAc: High-lift moves to a configuration other than the one commanded, so the achieved lift/drag does not match the crew's intended and displayed configuration; take-off or landing performance is computed against a configuration the aircraft is not in.
rows.effCrew: Crew acts on the selected/annunciated configuration; a mismatch that misleads the performance computation increases workload and can invalidate the take-off or landing speed schedule.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD supports that high-lift position feeds the performance computation, so an erroneous-vs-commanded configuration is a real misleading condition — but the magnitude of the resulting performance shortfall (e.g. runway/margin loss on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip) and whether it is detected before commit are not stated. Cannot derive a class without the achieved-vs-required performance delta.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment between sides
rows.effAc: Left/right high-lift mismatch produces a rolling and yawing moment at low speed; asymmetry brakes at each section exist specifically to arrest this. Uncontained asymmetry at low speed near the stall imposes a roll upset the aircraft may not have authority to counter in the take-off/landing configuration.
rows.effCrew: Immediate high-workload recovery from an asymmetry-induced roll/yaw at low speed and low altitude; degraded-configuration landing likely.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD shows asymmetry brakes are fitted at each section to protect against exactly this, indicating the designers treat asymmetry as a significant condition — but the protected (asymmetry-arrested) versus unprotected outcome, the residual roll authority in the take-off/landing config, and the low-speed margin are not quantified in the provided material. The class turns on whether asymmetry is arrested and residual controllability, which is not derivable here.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced high-lift configuration range or slower actuation
rows.effAc: High-lift still functions but cannot reach the full commanded range or actuates more slowly, so the achievable low-speed lift augmentation is reduced; approach and landing speeds increase and take-off/landing performance degrades against the semi-prepared strip requirement.
rows.effCrew: Crew flies a higher-speed degraded-configuration approach and landing with increased workload and reduced margin against the 1,800 m landing requirement.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction (higher approach/landing speeds, degraded performance) is grounded, but the magnitude of the configuration-range reduction and the resulting speed/distance penalty are not stated, so whether the reduced safety margin is significant (Major) or large (Hazardous) cannot be derived from the provided definition.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of one high-lift device group with remaining available
rows.effAc: One high-lift device group (e.g. a flap section or the slats) is lost while the remaining groups stay available; total lift augmentation is reduced and, if the loss is one-sided, an asymmetry may be introduced. Approach/landing speeds rise and performance degrades relative to full high-lift.
rows.effCrew: Crew flies a degraded-configuration approach at higher speed with increased workload; asymmetry brakes contain any side-to-side mismatch from a one-sided group loss.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Whether one lost group is symmetric or one-sided, and the resulting lift/asymmetry and performance penalty, are not stated in the provided material; without the achieved-vs-required low-speed margin the reduction cannot be graded to a class.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift configuration capability (flaps/slats cannot be extended from the current position)
rows.effAc: With high-lift unavailable, take-off and approach/landing must be flown at a clean or partial configuration, raising stall and approach speeds and lengthening take-off and landing distance. Against a 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement and a ~1,080 m predicted rollout at max landing weight, the increased approach speed erodes the operating margin and risks a runway excursion on the semi-prepared strip; take-off field length is similarly increased.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload managing a higher-speed, longer-field approach and landing to a semi-prepared strip; non-normal configuration procedures and performance recomputation required.
rows.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.

Proposed as Hazardous pending the runway-length/speed-margin performance analysis, which is not in the SDD; if that analysis shows the excursion is unrecoverable at destination weights the class could rise, so confirm. rows.fcDesc: Erroneous gear position or downlock indication (indication does not reflect the true gear/downlock state)
rows.effCrew: Crew may act on false gear-down/locked indication and land with a gear not locked, or reject a sound configuration on a false unsafe indication; either mis-sets the aircraft for a semi-prepared-strip landing.

Effect-on-aircraft and severity left blank pending that determination.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded gear movement (gear retracts or extends without a crew command)
rows.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.

Cannot state effect-on-aircraft or classify; left blank per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced footprint flotation on semi-prepared surface (footprint pressure exceeds what the operating surface can bear)
rows.effAc: Footprint pressure higher than the semi-prepared surface tolerates risks gear rutting, sinkage or bogie damage during rollout and taxi on the unprepared strip, degrading directional control and braking effectiveness and potentially immobilising or damaging the aircraft on the surface.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload maintaining directional control and managing braking/steering on a degrading surface; possible immobilisation requiring recovery.
rows.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Flotation is the specific reason the gear is sized from a tactical airlifter, and reduced flotation defeats a design purpose on the semi-prepared strip — but the aircraft-level severity depends on how far footprint pressure exceeds surface bearing capacity and whether the outcome is a controllable slow-taxi degradation or a loss of control/sinkage event. That surface-bearing/footprint margin is not quantified in the SDD, so severity is left blank rather than guessed.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of downlock confirmation on one unit (downlock sensing unavailable on a single gear unit while gear is mechanically down)
rows.effCrew: Crew cannot confirm downlock on one unit and must apply the associated non-normal procedure (e.g. alternate confirmation or gear cycling) before committing to a semi-prepared-strip landing; increased workload and possible diversion/hold.
rows.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Dual independent downlock sensing per unit is described; loss of downlock CONFIRMATION on one unit is a loss of indication, not necessarily of the locked state. The aircraft-level effect turns on whether an independent confirmation means exists and the consequence of landing with unconfirmed (but possibly locked) gear — not derivable from the function definition alone, so effect-on-aircraft and severity are left blank.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground support / flotation capability
rows.effAc: On landing or take-off roll the aircraft is not supported on its gear or the footprint sinks/collapses on the semi-prepared surface; loss of the aircraft is credible with structural collapse and potential fire from adjacent fuel/hydraulic runs.
rows.effCrew: Sudden loss of ground contact/attitude with no recovery available on the ground; crew cannot compensate.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of ground support/flotation during ground roll leads to airframe collapse and probable loss of the aircraft; effects support the highest class. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded braking with no crew command
rows.effAc: Uncommanded braking during the take-off roll or landing rollout produces unexpected deceleration and, if asymmetric, a directional excursion off the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip; tyre/brake damage and potential departure from the prepared surface.
rows.effCrew: Crew faced with unexpected deceleration/veer requiring immediate corrective steering and thrust management.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect spans a directional excursion (potentially severe) to a rejected take-off nuisance; the provided function definition does not state whether uncommanded braking is symmetric or asymmetric, nor the resulting excursion magnitude on the strip, so the driving effect and its worst-phase class cannot be grounded — engineering assessment of excursion and overrun needed.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous braking response to pedal command
rows.effAc: Braking effort does not match the commanded pedal input (too much, too little, or wrong wheels), degrading achievable deceleration against the 1,080 m predicted rollout / 1,800 m requirement margin and risking an overrun or directional excursion on the semi-prepared surface.
rows.effCrew: Crew cannot achieve expected stopping performance from pedal input; increased workload to manage rollout and steering.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect ranges from a manageable performance shortfall within the ~720 m margin to an overrun/excursion; the function definition does not state the magnitude of the erroneous response or its symmetry, so the worst-phase driving effect and its class cannot be grounded — braking-performance and overrun assessment needed.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric braking between left and right
rows.effAc: Differential left/right braking during the rollout or reject yaws the aircraft, and on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip with ~1,080 m rollout the excursion can carry the aircraft off the prepared surface with gear/structural damage.
rows.effCrew: Crew must apply immediate directional correction (steering, differential thrust) under high workload to keep the aircraft on the strip.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Directional excursion from asymmetric braking on a semi-prepared strip is credibly a large reduction in safety margin, but the function definition does not quantify the asymmetry or the crew's ability to counter it, so the worst-phase class cannot be committed — directional-control and controllability assessment needed.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Undetected asymmetric braking developing below detection threshold
rows.effAc: A slow-developing left/right braking imbalance below the detection/annunciation threshold is uncorrected, so the aircraft drifts off centreline during rollout before the crew or anti-skid intervene, risking a runway/strip excursion on the semi-prepared surface.
rows.effCrew: Crew unaware of the developing imbalance and take no early corrective action; correction begins only once the drift becomes noticeable, reducing available reaction margin.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The undetected case removes early crew correction and can worsen the excursion versus the annunciated case, but the function definition does not state the imbalance magnitude reachable below threshold nor the resulting excursion, so the driving effect and its class cannot be grounded — detection-threshold and excursion assessment needed.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced wheel braking effectiveness (partial loss of braking, still available at degraded capability)
rows.effAc: Deceleration performance degraded; the ~720 m margin between the 1,800 m landing requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared surface is reduced, raising risk of overrun on the fixed-length strip.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload managing rollout; crew relies on remaining braking, reversers (inboard only) and any autobrake degradation annunciation.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in the landing/RTO safety margin on a fixed-length semi-prepared strip, with braking retained via dual hydraulic supply and accumulator reserve; proposed for engineer confirmation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of anti-skid protection with braking retained
rows.effAc: Wheel braking available but without per-wheel-pair anti-skid modulation; risk of tyre skid/lock-up and degraded deceleration on the semi-prepared (potentially contaminated) surface.
rows.effCrew: Crew must modulate braking manually to avoid skid; increased workload on a fixed-length strip.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Braking is retained, but the SDD does not quantify the deceleration penalty or skid/directional-control consequence of anti-skid loss on a semi-prepared surface; without that effect the aircraft-level severity cannot be derived. Needs anti-skid-off stopping performance and directional-control data.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of one wheel-pair braking (braking retained on remaining wheels)
rows.effAc: Braking capacity reduced by the affected wheel pair; potential mild braking asymmetry and reduced total deceleration, eroding the ~720 m landing/RTO margin on the fixed-length semi-prepared strip.
rows.effCrew: Crew manages residual asymmetry with steering/differential braking; increased workload on rollout.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in braking capability/safety margin on a fixed-length strip with substantial residual braking retained (20 tyres across six main bogies); proposed for engineer confirmation. Asymmetry magnitude from a single wheel pair not quantified in the SDD. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Undetected reduced braking effectiveness (degradation developing below crew detection threshold)
rows.effAc: Actual braking capability lower than the crew believes; on a fixed-length semi-prepared strip with a ~720 m margin, an unannounced deficit removes the crew's ability to plan for the true stopping distance and raises overrun risk.
rows.effCrew: Crew continues normal duties with no action taken (unaware); no cue to select alternate braking, delay, or plan a go-around.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Large reduction in the landing/RTO safety margin because the deficit is undetected on a fixed-length strip, removing crew compensation; proposed as Hazardous for engineer confirmation, contingent on substantiating that the degradation is genuinely undetected and its magnitude relative to the ~720 m margin. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel braking capability
rows.effAc: No wheel braking beyond the accumulator reserve (sized for six full brake applications with all three hydraulic systems lost); on a 1,800 m fixed-length semi-prepared strip against ~1,080 m predicted rollout, high risk of overrun with only reverser (inboard) and aerodynamic deceleration remaining.
rows.effCrew: Crew applies accumulator/emergency braking, reversers and directional control to arrest the aircraft within the strip; high workload and reduced margin.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Large reduction in functional capability and safety margin on a fixed-length semi-prepared strip, mitigated by accumulator reserve (six applications) and inboard reversers; proposed as Hazardous. Overrun outcome severity (potential loss of airplane) is not established strongly enough in the SDD to commit Catastrophic — needs overrun-consequence analysis to confirm the class. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded nose-wheel steering deflection
rows.effAc: Uncommanded nose-gear deflection introduces an unintended directional input during ground roll; on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against ~1,080 m predicted rollout, a deflection can cause runway departure or loss of directional control on the ground.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded input and counter it with pedal/tiller and differential braking; increased workload during a high-speed ground phase.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects on the aircraft (potential runway/strip departure during ground roll) are stated, but the magnitude and rate of an uncommanded deflection and the available crew counter authority are not defined in the SDD, so whether the outcome is a directional excursion the crew can contain (Major) or an uncontrollable departure (Hazardous/Catastrophic) cannot be derived from the provided material. Confirm deflection authority and crew override before committing a class.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous steering response to crew command
rows.effAc: Steering responds in the wrong direction or with the wrong gain to a crew command, producing a directional error during ground roll on a semi-prepared strip with limited rollout margin.
rows.effCrew: Crew commands steering and receives an unexpected response; must recognise the mismatch and revert to pedals/differential braking; increased workload in a high-speed ground phase.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.

Confirm response-error bounds and crew reversion means before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced nose-wheel steering authority
rows.effAc: Reduced steering authority leaves less directional control on the ground; on a semi-prepared strip the aircraft can still be steered but with reduced precision, degrading control margin during rollout.
rows.effCrew: Crew compensates with rudder (at speed) and differential braking; slight-to-moderate increase in workload during ground manoeuvring and rollout.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Confirm residual authority before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose-wheel steering capability
rows.effAc: No nose-wheel steering; directional control on the ground relies on rudder at speed and differential braking. Low-speed manoeuvring on the ground is severely degraded; on a semi-prepared strip directional control during rollout depends wholly on the braking system.
rows.effCrew: Crew maintains the ground track by rudder and differential braking; increased workload, particularly at low speed and during turns.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Whether the residual means keeps this at Minor/Major cannot be derived from the provided material; confirm ground-controllability with steering lost before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Nose cargo door fails to reach fully closed position (SF-010 malfunction)
rows.effAc: Door not fully closed; per SDD the door forms part of the pressure boundary and forward fuselage structural load path when closed, so full closure is a precondition of pressurised flight.
rows.effCrew: Lock status is displayed on the flight deck at all times and is included in the take-off configuration check; crew has indication to detect and reject an improperly closed door before dispatch.
rows.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupants affected.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of primary (hydraulic) nose door drive with electric backup drive available (SF-010 partial loss)
rows.effAc: Door opened and closed hydraulically from system A with an electric backup drive; loss of primary drive is covered by the backup, door operation retained.

rows.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupants affected.

The consequence is a turnaround/dispatch matter whose severity is not derivable from the description — left blank.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose door open/close capability (SF-010 total loss)
rows.effAc: Door cannot be opened or closed by any means; if it fails closed the aircraft cannot be loaded/unloaded; if it fails open the aircraft cannot be dispatched (door is pressure boundary and forward load path when closed).
rows.effCrew: Ground operation only; the door cannot be operated in flight, so this is a ground/dispatch condition, not a flight event.
rows.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupants affected.

Whether a failed-closed vs failed-open state drives any airworthiness (as opposed to dispatch/availability) severity needs engineering judgement — left blank rather than reaching for the benign end.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous confirmation of a lock state not achieved — door indicated locked/secure while pins not fully engaged (SF-011 malfunction, latent)
rows.effAc: Door is part of the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path when closed; an undetected unlocked/partially-locked door misrepresented as secure could compromise the pressure boundary and forward load path in pressurised flight. The SDD does not state the resulting aircraft-level outcome.
rows.effCrew: Dual dissimilar lock sensing (proximity harness plus mechanical indicator) and the take-off configuration monitor are the defences; erroneous confirmation defeats the primary sensing indication, potentially leaving the crew unaware.

Severity must be derived from a stated aircraft effect, which the provided material does not give — abstaining per the abstention rule rather than assuming Catastrophic.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous unlock permission granted with hold pressurised — pressure interlock defeated (SF-011 malfunction)
rows.effAc: Design intent: the door cannot be opened with the hold pressurised — a pressure interlock vents and confirms residual differential below 0.1 psi before the lock actuator will run. Erroneous unlock permission with the hold pressurised would defeat that interlock; the SDD does not state the resulting aircraft-level outcome.
rows.effCrew: Door is operated only from the ground handling panel with the aircraft on jacks or gear and cannot be operated in flight; the interlock is the protecting feature against unlocking against a differential.
rows.effPax: Hold not occupied in flight; no occupants affected.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity is not derivable from the provided material — left blank.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous lock-secure confirmation presented to the crew with the nose visor not fully locked (crew unaware, continue normal duties)
rows.effAc: Nose visor forms the forward pressure boundary and forward-fuselage structural load path when closed; an unlocked-but-confirmed-secure state removes assurance of that load path and pressure boundary. Under pressurisation and flight loads a not-fully-locked single-load-path visor can release, with loss of pressure boundary integrity and forward structure.

Severity rationale: Effects stated (loss of forward pressure boundary and single-load-path structure with no crew awareness) support Catastrophic; door is 'part of the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path when closed' and 'a single load path … treated as structure'. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced locking redundancy or loss of a single lock-sensing path, with locking and confirmation still available

rows.fcDesc: Loss of one of the two dissimilar lock-sensing paths, with the other sensing path retained
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants in the affected volume.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose-door closure locking and confirmation of lock state
rows.effAc: With no locking and no confirmation, there is no assurance the visor is secured as the forward pressure boundary and forward-fuselage structural load path; a not-fully-locked single-load-path visor can release under pressurisation and flight loads, with loss of pressure boundary integrity and forward structure.

rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants in the affected volume.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous restraint locking: restraint mechanically locked and indicated engaged but not carrying rated longitudinal load
rows.effAc: A single blade of up to 72.6 t restrained by saddle straps not carrying rated longitudinal load risks blade movement under flight/ground load cases, with consequent centre-of-gravity shift and potential structural overload of the hold hard points; the aircraft-level severity of the resulting shift is not determinable from the function definition alone.

Severity left empty pending that load-redistribution and CG assessment.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of longitudinal payload restraint
rows.effAc: Unrestrained 72.6 t single blade free to shift longitudinally under acceleration/deceleration and manoeuvre loads; large uncontrolled CG excursion beyond controllable limits and potential structural overload of hold floor beam / hard points and airframe.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced longitudinal restraint capacity at one or more stations
rows.effAc: Reduced restraint margin at one or more stations; design states loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, so single-station capacity reduction is reacted with reduced margin rather than immediate load shift; risk of progression to load movement if multiple stations degrade.

Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced restraint tension below required at one or more stations
rows.effAc: Strap tension below required at one or more stations reduces the pre-load holding the blade; loss of tension on any strap is annunciated; a single under-tensioned station is within the neighbour-reaction design but reduces margin against load movement.

rows.effAc: Restraint indicates/locks as secured while not carrying rated longitudinal load; with the crew unaware and taking no action, blade is effectively unrestrained under longitudinal loads at one or more stations, risking a CG excursion and structural overload as loads develop — approaching the total-loss consequence undetected.

Proposed pending confirmation of how much of the load path is defeated when 'locked but not loaded'. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded pitch authority within manoeuvre limits
rows.effAc: Reduced pitch control authority or rate while manoeuvring capability remains within manoeuvre limits; reduced margin to the pitch envelope, potentially requiring larger inputs or restricted manoeuvring.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded pitch authority developing below detection threshold
rows.effAc: Pitch authority erodes below the crew's detection threshold; the crew is unaware and takes no action, so the degradation is uncovered until it manifests as loss of adequate pitch control at a high-demand point (e.g. flare or upset recovery).

rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of one of two independent downlock sensing circuits per unit is a significant reduction in the assurance of a safety-critical configuration but leaves an independent confirmation path available; a significant reduction in safety margin / increase in workload rather than a large one. Confirm against the effect of landing on single-sensed downlock and any dispatch limitation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground support / flotation capability
rows.effAc: Aircraft not supported on its gear / footprint pressure not spread; collapse or sink-in on the semi-prepared surface. Loss of the load path that absorbs landing and taxi loads and spreads footprint pressure to the level the operating surface requires. Directional control and braking, which depend on gear-borne wheels, are lost with it.
rows.effCrew: Loss of ground controllability with no available means to arrest the aircraft; abnormal/emergency situation.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only (nominal two).
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the sole means of supporting the aircraft on a semi-prepared surface at touchdown/rollout, with directional control and braking dependent on it, plausibly leads to loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded braking with no crew command
rows.effAc: Uncommanded wheel braking with no crew command; potential asymmetric retardation and directional upset, and reduced take-off acceleration / loss of predicted rollout margin (1,800 m required vs ~1,080 m predicted). Brake overheat and tyre damage on the semi-prepared surface.
rows.effCrew: Unexpected retardation and possible directional excursion during a high-energy ground phase; increased workload to detect and counter.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only (nominal two).
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states normal/alternate braking supply and anti-skid per wheel pair but does not quantify the uncommanded braking magnitude, how many wheels/bogies are affected, or the directional/energy consequence during take-off vs taxi; without that the aircraft effect cannot be bounded, so severity is left empty.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous braking response to pedal command
rows.effAc: Wheel braking that differs from the crew's pedal command (more, less, or delayed retardation than intended), degrading the ability to stop within the required landing distance on the semi-prepared surface, against a margin of 1,800 m required vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout.
rows.effCrew: Braking response does not match pedal input; crew must detect and compensate during a high-energy ground phase.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only (nominal two).
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD does not state the sign or magnitude of the error (over- vs under-braking) nor the residual capability via alternate supply/accumulator/anti-skid for this erroneous-response case; the aircraft stopping-distance effect cannot be derived, so severity is left empty.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric braking between left and right
rows.effAc: Unequal left/right wheel braking produces a yawing moment and lateral directional excursion during ground roll, risking a runway/strip departure on the unpaved semi-prepared surface where lateral margin is limited.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect the asymmetry and counter with steering/rudder to hold the centreline during a high-energy ground phase; increased workload.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only (nominal two).
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD notes anti-skid operates per wheel pair and A/B brake supply but does not quantify the asymmetry magnitude, the counter authority of nose-wheel steering/rudder, or the resulting excursion; the aircraft directional consequence cannot be bounded, so severity is left empty.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Undetected asymmetric braking developing below detection threshold
rows.effAc: Left/right braking asymmetry that develops below the detection/annunciation threshold and is not presented to the crew, so no timely correction is applied and a slow directional divergence builds during ground roll on the semi-prepared surface.
rows.effCrew: Crew continue normally with no annunciation; the asymmetry is not detected until the directional divergence is manifest, compressing available reaction time.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only (nominal two).
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD does not define a braking-asymmetry detection threshold or annunciation for LDG (weight-on-wheels/wheel-speed go to avionics but no asymmetry-detection function is described); the undetected divergence magnitude and the crew reaction window cannot be derived, so severity is left empty.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced wheel braking effectiveness (partial loss of wheel braking)
rows.effAc: Reduced deceleration on the ground; landing rollout increases against the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement, eroding the margin over the ~1,080 m predicted rollout; higher risk of runway/strip overrun at max landing weight.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload managing deceleration; crew supplements with inboard reverse thrust and directional control; degraded-braking annunciation actioned.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in ground deceleration margin against a tight 1,800 m vs ~1,080 m landing-distance budget, with reverse thrust and remaining margin available as compensation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of anti-skid protection with braking retained
rows.effAc: Braking retained but without per-wheel-pair skid protection; on a semi-prepared surface, wheel lock-up and reduced achieved deceleration are likely, degrading stopping performance and directional control against the landing-distance margin.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload modulating braking manually to avoid skid; crew adapts technique for the surface; anti-skid failure annunciated.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in achievable deceleration and directional-control margin on a semi-prepared surface where skid protection is most needed, with manual modulation available as compensation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of one wheel-pair braking
rows.effAc: Braking lost at one wheel pair produces asymmetric and reduced total braking; deceleration margin against the 1,800 m requirement erodes and a directional (yaw) tendency must be countered during rollout.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload correcting for asymmetric braking through steering/rudder and differential technique; affected-wheel annunciation actioned.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in deceleration and directional-control margin from asymmetric braking on a semi-prepared surface, with steering and remaining brakes as compensation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Undetected reduced braking effectiveness (crew unaware)
rows.effAc: Braking effectiveness reduced without annunciation; crew commit to the strip believing full braking is available, so no compensating technique is applied and achieved deceleration falls short of planned; consequence against the 1,800 m vs ~1,080 m margin cannot be established without landing-performance analysis.
rows.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action, unaware of the degradation.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a class: the undetected case removes crew compensation, but whether the reduced deceleration produces an overrun (potentially Hazardous) or stays within the ~720 m margin depends on quantitative landing-performance analysis not provided. Amount of undetected reduction is also unspecified. Leaving severity empty rather than guessing.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel braking capability
rows.effAc: No wheel braking from normal or alternate hydraulic supply; deceleration relies on accumulator-supported emergency braking (sized for six full applications with all three systems lost), inboard reverse thrust and aerodynamic drag; overrun of the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip is a credible outcome at max landing weight, more so on a rejected take-off.
rows.effCrew: High workload executing emergency/accumulator braking and reverse-thrust deceleration; directional control by steering; large reduction in stopping-performance safety margin.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Large reduction in stopping-performance safety margin with credible strip overrun, mitigated by accumulator emergency braking (six applications), inboard reversers and the landing-distance margin, so proposed Hazardous rather than Catastrophic absent an overrun/energy analysis substantiating loss of the airplane. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded nose-wheel steering deflection
rows.effAc: Uncommanded steering deflection produces a lateral runway excursion tendency at speed; on a semi-prepared 1,800 m strip with ~1,080 m predicted rollout the lateral margin to leave the prepared surface is limited. Crew must counter with rudder/differential braking; a departure from the surface at speed risks gear collapse or airframe damage.
rows.effCrew: Sudden directional upset demands immediate corrective input with differential braking and rudder; high, time-critical workload during a high-speed ground phase.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect plausibly ranges from Major (controllable excursion tendency countered by differential braking/rudder) to Hazardous (departure from a narrow semi-prepared surface at speed); the SDD does not quantify nose-wheel steering authority versus the crew's residual directional means on the operating surface, so the class cannot be derived from the provided function definition alone. Confirm against ground directional-control sizing.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous steering response to crew command
rows.effAc: Steering responds in the wrong sense or magnitude to tiller/pedal command, opposing the crew's intended track; on a narrow semi-prepared strip this drives a lateral excursion tendency the crew must recognise and counter before departing the surface.
rows.effCrew: Crew command produces an opposite or exaggerated aircraft response, requiring rapid recognition and reversal via differential braking and rudder; high workload with recognition delay a factor.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Erroneous (mis-sensed) response could be more severe than a symmetric uncommanded deflection because the crew's initial input aggravates the excursion; the SDD does not quantify authority or the recognition/reversion path, so the class cannot be derived here. Confirm against ground directional-control analysis.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced nose-wheel steering authority
rows.effAc: Reduced steering authority leaves the aircraft trackable but with less directional margin; crew supplements with rudder (aerodynamically effective at speed) and differential braking. On a semi-prepared strip the reduced margin narrows the crew's ability to correct crosswind and surface-induced drift.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload to hold centreline using rudder and differential braking; degraded but manageable directional control.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Likely Minor-to-Major depending on residual authority and crosswind exposure on the operating surface; the SDD does not state the degraded steering authority level or the crosswind case, so the class cannot be derived. Confirm against ground directional-control margins.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose-wheel steering capability
rows.effAc: No nose-wheel steering; directional control on the ground relies on rudder (effective only above a speed threshold) and differential braking. At low taxi speed the aircraft may be undirectable without towing; during high-speed roll on a narrow semi-prepared strip the loss of the low-speed directional means reduces the margin against a lateral excursion in a crosswind.
rows.effCrew: Crew directs the aircraft by differential braking and rudder alone; increased workload, particularly at low speed and in crosswind, with a manageable path if differential braking retains authority.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on whether differential braking plus rudder provides adequate directional control on the semi-prepared surface across the speed range and crosswind envelope; the SDD does not establish that residual capability, so a class cannot be derived. Confirm against ground directional-control sizing and the crosswind case.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded door movement
rows.effAc: The nose visor forms the pressure boundary and part of the forward fuselage structural load path when closed, and cannot be operated in flight. Uncommanded movement on the ground during or after loading unlatches/moves a primary structural and pressure-boundary element; if it moved with the aircraft dispatching, the pressure boundary and forward load path would be compromised. On the ground the direct hazard is to ground personnel and to the aircraft from an unrestrained ~nose-section movement.
rows.effCrew: Loss of a confirmed door-locked state; crew must detect via the dual dissimilar lock sensing and the take-off configuration check and not dispatch; workload to diagnose and secure.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only. Ground-personnel exposure during loading is an occupational/ground-safety consideration outside the airborne occupant set.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The uncommanded-movement condition is bounded on the ground by the in-flight-operation inhibit and detected by dual dissimilar lock sensing plus the take-off configuration check; whether it is caught before dispatch (crew-aware) or not drives the class, and the SDD does not establish the airborne consequence of an undetected unlocked/moving visor. The severity turns on the detection/dispatch-inhibit effectiveness, which must be confirmed; class not derivable from the function definition alone.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Nose cargo door fails to reach fully closed position (malfunction of open/close capability)
rows.effAc: Door not fully closed; pressure boundary and forward fuselage load path not established. Detected on ground before dispatch via lock/position status in the take-off configuration check.
rows.effCrew: Take-off configuration check flags door not closed/locked; dispatch withheld until resolved.
rows.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight and no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Grounded as a ground-phase condition detected before dispatch (§5.7.6 door 'cannot be operated in flight'; lock status 'included in the take-off configuration check'). The SDD supports a dispatch-inhibit outcome but does not establish an in-flight aircraft effect from this condition, and any severity depends on the crew-detection/dispatch operational case, which is not stated here. Left empty for engineer to classify against the take-off configuration/dispatch analysis.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of primary door drive with backup drive available (partial loss of nose door open/close capability)
rows.effAc: Primary hydraulic (system A) door drive lost; electric backup drive available to open/close the door. No effect on flight; door operated only on the ground.
rows.effCrew: Ground handling reverts to backup drive; turnaround time may increase.
rows.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight and no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Grounded: SDD states the door 'is opened and closed hydraulically from system A with an electric backup drive' and 'cannot be operated in flight' (§5.7.2, §5.7.6), so a partial loss with backup available is a ground-only degradation. The SDD does not establish an aircraft-level flight effect and any severity turns on the ground/turnaround operational impact, which is not quantified here. Left empty for engineer to classify.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose door open/close capability
rows.effAc: Neither primary nor backup drive available; door cannot be opened or closed. If already closed and locked, flight is unaffected; if open, aircraft cannot be dispatched. No in-flight aircraft effect as the door is not operated in flight.
rows.effCrew: Loading/unloading prevented; dispatch withheld until door state resolved.
rows.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight and no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Grounded: door 'cannot be operated in flight' and is operated only from the ground handling panel (§5.7.6). The SDD supports a ground dispatch/availability outcome but does not establish an in-flight aircraft-level effect for total loss of open/close capability. Severity depends on the operational/dispatch case, which is not stated. Left empty for engineer.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced locking redundancy or a single lock-sensing path lost
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD states dual dissimilar independently routed lock sensing (§5.7.2), but does not state the aircraft-level effect of losing one path with locking still achieved and the second path confirming; the resulting effect (latent condition, dispatch impact, exposure) is engineering judgment not grounded in the description. Severity left empty pending effect assessment.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of one of two dissimilar lock-sensing paths
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — With one of two dissimilar sensing paths lost, the SDD indicates the remaining path (proximity harness or mechanical indicator) may still confirm lock state; the aircraft-level effect and any latent-fault exposure argument are not stated in the description. Severity left empty pending effect assessment.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of longitudinal payload restraint
rows.effAc: With no longitudinal restraint the single 72.6 t blade is free to translate along the 108 m hold under acceleration, deceleration, pitch and gust loads; the resulting large-mass shift along the aircraft axis can drive the centre of gravity outside the certified envelope and impose loads the hold floor beam structure and hard points were not sized to react in an unrestrained case, with potential to breach the pressure boundary.
rows.effCrew: Restraint condition annunciated via the tension monitoring loop; crew have indication only, no in-flight adjustment of restraint is available, so no crew action can arrest a shifting blade.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncontained longitudinal shift of the full 72.6 t design payload along the pitch axis can drive the aircraft outside its CoG/structural envelope with potential loss of control and loss of the airplane; effects support Catastrophic. PROPOSED for engineer confirmation — depends on the loads/CoG analysis (not in the SDD) establishing that an unrestrained shift exceeds the controllable envelope. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Restraint mechanically locked but not carrying rated tension (undetected)
rows.effAc: The restraint is mechanically locked but does not carry rated load and the shortfall is not detected; under flight and ground load cases the blade can move within the slack, so that a load path assumed present is absent, permitting a large-mass longitudinal shift of the 72.6 t blade with the same envelope and structural consequences as loss of restraint, without prior indication.
rows.effCrew: Crew unaware: continue duties normally, tension loop shows a valid/locked state, no crew action taken because no shortfall is annunciated.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A latent, undetected failure of the restraint to carry rated tension can produce the same uncontained longitudinal shift of the full payload as complete loss, with no warning; effects support Catastrophic.
