PROPOSED for engineer confirmation — depends on confirming (a) the loads/CoG analysis and (b) that the monitoring loop cannot distinguish 'locked' from 'locked but not tensioned'. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced longitudinal restraint capacity at one or more stations
rows.effAc: Longitudinal restraint capacity is reduced at one or more stations; the SDD states load paths are sized so that loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, so a single-station reduction is reacted by adjacent stations, but the aircraft-level margin lost and the number of stations at which capacity must degrade before restraint is inadequate is not established in the provided material.
rows.effCrew: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight; loss on two adjacent stations is annunciated as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention. Crew have indication only, no in-flight adjustment.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive an aircraft effect from the provided material: the SDD establishes single-station redundancy (neighbours carry the load) but does not quantify how much restraint margin is lost, or at how many stations degradation defeats restraint of the 72.6 t blade. Without that the residual longitudinal-shift risk and its envelope consequence cannot be stated, so severity is left blank pending the restraint sizing / loads analysis.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced restraint tension below required at one or more stations
rows.effAc: Restraint tension falls below the required value at one or more stations while the restraint remains engaged; slack in the affected straps permits limited longitudinal movement of the blade before adjacent stations react load, but the aircraft-level consequence of the resulting movement is not quantifiable from the provided material.
rows.effCrew: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated; loss on two adjacent stations is annunciated as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention. Crew have indication only.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive an aircraft effect: the SDD gives the annunciation thresholds but not how much longitudinal blade movement an under-tension (but engaged) condition permits, nor whether that movement affects CoG/structural margins. Severity left blank pending the restraint sizing / loads analysis that establishes the tolerable tension shortfall.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric forward thrust across the aircraft (uncommanded thrust split between sides)
rows.effAc: Yawing/rolling moment from a thrust split; at the 28 m outboard moment arm the directional-control demand is the sizing case, consuming rudder authority and degrading trajectory control, worst around take-off/low speed.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect the asymmetry, identify the affected side and counter with rudder/thrust reduction; increased workload at a critical phase.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect magnitude spans from a manageable trim asymmetry to a large reduction in safety margins at V1; the function definition alone does not fix WHICH — the split magnitude, the phase, and available rudder authority determine whether this is Major (MAJ-1) or Hazardous (HAZ-1). Left empty pending the amount/type of asymmetry and the directional-control margin substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced available forward thrust (partial loss, e.g. one engine or degraded output, symmetric or single-engine)
rows.effAc: Reduced thrust available; loss of one engine at/after V1 is a designed continuation case with reduced climb performance and increased asymmetry demand handled by rudder authority; safety margins reduced.
rows.effCrew: Crew execute engine-out procedure, manage asymmetry and continue to a suitable aerodrome; increased workload.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — 'Reduced available forward thrust' covers a range from a minor single-engine derate (aircraft designed to continue — Major/MAJ-1) to multiple-engine loss on one side, explicitly retained as a condition to be studied and outside the dispatch case. The definition does not fix the amount of reduction, so the driving effect and class cannot be established; left empty pending the degree of thrust loss.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of forward thrust generation (no forward thrust available by any means)
rows.effAc: Aircraft cannot sustain flight; forced descent and off-field/uncontrolled landing with loss of the airplane and multiple fatalities credible.
rows.effCrew: Crew cannot restore thrust; forced descent regardless of action.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; loss of the airplane implies loss of the flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of all forward thrust in flight leaves no means to sustain flight and leads to loss of the airplane and multiple fatalities — CAT-1. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command
rows.effAc: Aircraft rolls other than as commanded (wrong sense or wrong magnitude), producing an unintended bank and a reduction in lateral safety margin; potential for large attitude excursion.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter the erroneous response, imposing significant to excessive workload; recovery difficulty depends on the erroneous authority and the flight phase.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An erroneous roll response is a large reduction in safety margins with excessive crew workload to counter it (HAZ-1/HAZ-2). CONFIRM: the FCS command-authority limiting — if erroneous roll authority is unbounded (loss of control, especially at low altitude), this reaches Catastrophic; if effectively bounded and countered, it may be lower. Classify against the worst applicable phase. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded roll authority remaining within required manoeuvre limits
rows.effAc: Reduced roll authority, but the aircraft can still perform the required manoeuvres within limits; a reduction in safety margin without loss of a required capability.
rows.effCrew: Slightly increased crew workload to fly with the reduced authority; degraded law annunciated.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: The condition is defined as roll authority still within required manoeuvre limits, so no required manoeuvre capability is lost; the effect is a significant reduction in safety margin / functional capability with a modest workload increase, which supports Major (MAJ-1). Proposed for engineering confirmation. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded roll authority reduced outside required manoeuvre limits
rows.effAc: Roll authority reduced below that required for the manoeuvre envelope; a required manoeuvre capability is no longer available, a large reduction in functional capability, most critical in the engine-out / blade-loaded directional-control case.
rows.effCrew: Significantly increased workload and difficulty; crew constrained to reduced manoeuvring, potentially unable to counter a disturbance requiring full authority.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Defined as roll authority outside required manoeuvre limits, i.e. a required manoeuvre capability is lost — a large reduction in functional capability with excessive crew difficulty, supporting Hazardous (HAZ-1). The engine-out with maximum blade payload is the SDD directional-control sizing case, reinforcing criticality. Proposed for engineering confirmation; the manoeuvre-limit margin is not quantified in the SDD. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous confirmation of a lock state not achieved (misleading lock indication with door not fully locked)
rows.effAc: Crew and take-off configuration monitor are shown a locked/secure state that has not been achieved; door proceeds to flight not fully locked. Latches may back-drive and the visor — the entire nose section and part of the pressure boundary and forward fuselage load path — is at risk of opening/departing in flight, with associated loss of pressure boundary and structural load path.
rows.effCrew: No warning of the unsafe lock state; crew continue normal duties (misleading indication defeats the take-off configuration check). No timely corrective action available.
rows.effPax: None carried; hold unoccupied.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. The door 'forms part of the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path when closed' (§5.7.1) and dual dissimilar sensing exists precisely to prevent a false lock confirmation; a false confirmation defeats that protection and the take-off configuration check, so the aircraft flies with an unlocked single-load-path nose visor at risk of in-flight opening/departure — loss of the airplane. Effects support CAT-1 (loss of the airplane). Engineer to confirm against the structural/pressure-boundary special-condition case. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous unlock permission granted with the hold pressurised (lock/interlock malfunction)
rows.effAc: Unlock command permitted while the hold is pressurised, defeating the pressure interlock. Lock pins can be driven out with residual differential present; potential in-flight unlocking and opening/departure of the nose visor — loss of the pressure boundary and forward fuselage load path.
rows.effCrew: No protection from the interlock that normally blocks unlock above 0.1 psi residual differential; explosive/rapid opening possible with no effective crew mitigation.
rows.effPax: None carried; hold unoccupied.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED for confirmation. The interlock exists so the door 'cannot be opened with the hold pressurised' and confirms residual differential below 0.1 psi before the lock actuator will run (§5.7.2); erroneous unlock permission with the hold pressurised defeats that interlock and allows in-flight unlocking of a single-load-path pressure-boundary visor. Effects support CAT-1 (loss of the airplane). Engineer to confirm against the pressure-boundary special condition. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous lock-secure confirmation displayed with the nose door not fully locked (crew unaware)
rows.effAc: Nose visor is part of the pressure boundary and forward-fuselage load path when closed; a not-fully-locked door falsely confirmed as secure can open or fail in flight, breaching the pressure boundary and forward structural load path.
rows.effCrew: Crew accept the false lock confirmation at the take-off configuration check and continue normally; no corrective action taken until the boundary/structure fails.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants at risk directly, but loss of the airplane endangers flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected in-flight loss of the pressure boundary and forward-fuselage load path can lead to loss of the airplane; matches CAT-1 (loss of the airplane). [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose door-closure locking and confirmation
rows.effAc: With no locking achieved and no confirmation, the nose visor is not secured for flight; the door forms the pressure boundary and forward-fuselage load path when closed, so an unlocked door can open or depart in flight, breaching the boundary and forward structure.
rows.effCrew: Lock status is displayed and part of the take-off configuration check (§5.7.6), so complete loss of confirmation is expected to be detected on the ground and dispatch prevented; if departed unlocked, no recovery of the load path.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; loss of the airplane endangers flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of locking on a single-load-path pressure-boundary door, if not caught before flight, can lead to loss of the airplane; matches CAT-1. Note the take-off configuration check is a detection means, not a mitigation of the underlying condition — confirm exposure/detectability in the assessment. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous restraint locking — restraint mechanically locked but not carrying the rated load
rows.effAc: A single blade of up to 72.6 t that is not actually restrained to rated load can shift under flight/ground load cases, producing a large uncommanded CG excursion and structural overload of the hold hard points; longitudinal restraint must hold through all flight and ground load cases (§5.8.1).
rows.effCrew: Restraint is indication-only in flight with no in-flight adjustment (§5.8.6); if the erroneous lock is not annunciated as loss of tension, crew take no action and cannot recover restraint in flight.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; a shifting 72.6 t payload endangers the flight crew and the airplane.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An unrestrained 72.6 t single payload shifting in flight drives a large CG excursion and structural load path failure that can lead to loss of the airplane; matches CAT-1 (loss of the airplane). [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric forward thrust across the aircraft (uncommanded thrust split between engines)
rows.effAc: Uncommanded yawing and rolling moment; directional control is sized on an outboard-engine loss at the 28 m moment arm, so an asymmetry approaching that magnitude demands the full available rudder authority and, if uncountered, drives departure from controlled flight.
rows.effCrew: Sudden requirement for corrective rudder/roll input; increased workload to maintain heading and wings level; severity depends on magnitude and phase.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects as stated — uncommanded asymmetry up to the outboard-engine-out sizing case can exceed available directional-control authority and lead to loss of the aircraft. Suggested, not committed: confirm against the rudder-authority/asymmetry analysis and worst applicable phase. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous forward thrust not matching the commanded setting
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: this condition is not carried in the SF-001 FCIM and the SDD states no aircraft-level effect for thrust silently differing from the commanded value. Confirm the condition is intended and supply whether the error is symmetric or asymmetric, and its magnitude/aircraft effect, before a class can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of forward thrust generation (all engines)
rows.effAc: Total loss of propulsive thrust; the aircraft cannot sustain flight and is committed to a forced descent/off-airport landing.
rows.effCrew: Extreme workload managing an all-engine-out glide and forced landing.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects as stated — total loss of forward thrust in flight leads to loss of the aircraft. Suggested, not committed: confirm classification for the applicable phases. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded reverse thrust deployment
rows.effAc: In flight, deployment of an inboard reverser (defeating the WoW + radio-altimeter inhibit and sleeve lock) produces large asymmetric drag and a strong yawing moment, potentially exceeding available directional-control authority. On the ground below the assumed inhibit conditions the effect is a control/deceleration upset of lesser magnitude.
rows.effCrew: In flight, sudden large yaw requiring immediate maximum corrective input; high workload and possible loss of control. On ground, corrective steering/braking demand.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects as stated for the in-flight case — an uncommanded inboard reverser deployment can exceed directional-control authority and lead to loss of the aircraft; this leans on the deployment defeating the described in-flight inhibits. Suggested, not committed: confirm the in-flight case is credible against the WoW + radio-altimeter + mechanical-lock inhibit, and split ground vs in-flight if the SFHA warrants it. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground reverse thrust (both inboard reversers unavailable on landing rollout)
rows.effAc: No reverse deceleration available; deceleration relies wholly on wheel braking and spoilers. On a paved surface with the certified braking margin this is a reduction in stopping margin only; on the semi-prepared destination strip the operating margin between the 1,800 m requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout is reduced.
rows.effCrew: Crew loses an expected deceleration means; increased attention to braking and rollout distance, no emergency action beyond normal braking.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only and are not credited for the certified landing-distance requirement, which is sized by wheel braking; total loss reduces margin (slight reduction in safety margin, slight increase in workload) but does not by itself produce a large or significant reduction. Confirm against the landing-performance accountability of reverse thrust. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced ground reverse thrust (partial reverse authority available on landing rollout)
rows.effAc: Reduced reverse deceleration; stopping distance longer than with full reverse but supplemented by wheel braking and spoilers. Consumes part of the operating margin on the semi-prepared strip.
rows.effCrew: Crew perceives reduced deceleration; increased monitoring of rollout distance, normal braking applied.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial reverse is a smaller reduction in deceleration than the total-loss case; reverse thrust is not credited for the certified landing distance, so a partial loss is at most a slight reduction in safety margin with slight increase in workload. Confirm against landing-performance accountability. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on the ground (one inboard reverser producing more reverse than the other)
rows.effAc: Asymmetric reverse produces a yawing/turning moment during rollout that must be countered by rudder and nose-wheel steering. Magnitude of the upset and available runway to arrest it are not established by the function definition.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter the asymmetry with steering/rudder inputs during rollout.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: the directional upset from an asymmetric inboard reverser and whether the crew can arrest it within the remaining semi-prepared strip length is a ground-directional-control assessment not yet available. Needs the ground-handling / directional-control analysis to bound the aircraft effect before a class can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust developing below the detection threshold on the ground (crew unaware)
rows.effAc: An undetected asymmetric reverse condition produces a yawing moment the crew is not alerted to; deviation develops before any correction is applied. Resulting excursion depends on magnitude and remaining runway, neither established by the function definition.
rows.effCrew: Crew continues rollout normally with no alert; correction applied only once the deviation becomes perceptible, later than in the aware case.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: the unaware asymmetric case delays crew correction and its aircraft effect (directional excursion on a semi-prepared strip) requires the ground-directional-control assessment plus the detection-threshold characterisation. Left empty pending that analysis.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command
rows.effAc: Aircraft rolls in a manner different from that commanded (wrong magnitude, wrong direction, or uncommanded component); the resulting attitude excursion and its consequence depend on magnitude and flight phase, which the function definition does not bound.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect the erroneous response and counter it; workload and difficulty depend on the magnitude of the error.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive a single aircraft effect: 'erroneous roll response' spans a wide band from a bounded nuisance transient to an uncommanded roll upset, and the FCIM text bounds neither the error magnitude nor the critical flight phase. A severity requires the roll-control assessment to bound the worst-case erroneous response before a class can be committed.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded roll motion with no crew command (crew aware)
rows.effAc: Aircraft rolls without command, departing the intended attitude; crew become aware through attitude display and aircraft response and counter with opposing roll input, arresting the divergence at the cost of a manoeuvre and reduced roll margin for the remainder of the flight.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter an uncommanded upset with an immediate manual input; increased workload to maintain wings-level and manage the degraded state.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded roll the crew must actively counter, at low flight levels, is a large reduction in safety margins requiring compensating crew action; classified Hazardous. The amplitude/authority of the uncommanded motion is not bounded in the SDD, so confirm this is not Catastrophic at the worst phase. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded roll divergence below detection threshold (crew unaware)
rows.effAc: A slow uncommanded roll develops below the detection threshold; the crew, being unaware, take no corrective action and continue normally, so the divergence accumulates until it either self-annunciates or reaches a point where recovery margin is affected.
rows.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally and take no action; effect on workload arises only if and when the condition eventually manifests.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the effect turns on the divergence rate versus available recovery margin at the point of eventual manifestation, and the SDD gives no aircraft-level effect, divergence rate, or detection-threshold data to bound it. Severity left blank pending that data.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded roll authority within manoeuvre limits (crew aware)
rows.effAc: Roll authority is reduced but the aircraft remains controllable within its manoeuvre limits; the crew are annunciated of the degraded state and fly within the reduced envelope, giving a reduction in roll safety margin without loss of controllability.
rows.effCrew: Crew are aware of the degradation and manage the aircraft within the reduced envelope; increased attention and workload to stay within limits.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: By definition still within manoeuvre limits, so a significant reduction in safety margin without loss of control; classified Major. Confirm against the engine-out plus blade-loaded directional/roll sizing case, which the SDD names as sizing but does not quantify. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded roll authority outside manoeuvre limits (crew aware)
rows.effAc: Roll authority is reduced below that required for the manoeuvre envelope; controllability is impaired such that the aircraft cannot meet its required manoeuvre margin, potentially at the engine-out/blade-loaded sizing case; the crew are aware but have limited ability to compensate.
rows.effCrew: Crew must manage an aircraft with insufficient roll manoeuvre margin, with excessive workload to maintain a safe flight path.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of required roll manoeuvre margin is a large reduction in safety margins and functional capability; classified Hazardous. Confirm whether, at the worst phase and at the sizing case, the loss of manoeuvre margin escalates toward loss of the aircraft (Catastrophic); the SDD names the sizing case but does not quantify the residual authority. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded roll authority developing below detection threshold (crew unaware)
rows.effAc: Roll authority erodes below the detection threshold; the crew, being unaware, continue normally and do not compensate, so the aircraft is flown with a reduced roll margin it does not know it has until a manoeuvre demand or the condition manifests.
rows.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally and take no action; workload effect arises only if a manoeuvre demand exceeds the unannunciated reduced authority.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: severity depends on the residual roll margin at the point a manoeuvre demand or self-annunciation manifests, and on whether that coincides with a demanding phase or the sizing case — none of which the SDD quantifies. Severity left blank pending that data.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of roll control authority
rows.effAc: Aircraft cannot be controlled about the roll axis by any means; bank angle can no longer be commanded or arrested, leading to loss of lateral/directional control of the flight path.
rows.effCrew: Crew unable to control roll through inceptors; no reversion path restores roll authority (mechanical reversion is to stabiliser trim and lower rudder only, not roll).
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of a primary control axis with no means of continued controlled flight; effects support loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to crew command
rows.effAc: Pitch surfaces respond incorrectly to crew command (wrong sense or magnitude), producing an uncommanded flight-path excursion about the pitch axis that can exceed structural or manoeuvre limits.
rows.effCrew: Crew command produces an unexpected/opposite pitch response; recovery may be impossible if the erroneous response is large or persistent.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous response on a primary control axis can drive an unrecoverable flight-path excursion; effects support loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch motion with no command
rows.effAc: Pitch surface moves with no crew or autopilot command (hardover/runaway), producing an uncommanded flight-path excursion about the pitch axis that can exceed structural or manoeuvre limits.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter an uncommanded pitch input; a full-authority hardover at a critical phase may be uncounterable.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded full-authority motion on a primary control axis can drive an unrecoverable excursion; effects support loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded pitch divergence below detection threshold (crew unaware)
rows.effAc: A slow uncommanded pitch drift develops below the threshold at which it is detected/annunciated; with the crew continuing normal duties and taking no action, the divergence progresses to a significant flight-path excursion or a departure from the controllable envelope.
rows.effCrew: Crew are unaware and take no corrective action; by the time the divergence is recognised, safety margins may be substantially eroded and recovery workload high.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected slow pitch divergence, with no crew action assumed, can progress to an unrecoverable flight-path excursion; effects support loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded pitch authority within manoeuvre limits
rows.effAc: Pitch control remains available but at reduced authority; the aircraft can still be manoeuvred within the required manoeuvre limits, with a significant reduction in pitch capability/margin.
rows.effCrew: Crew retain pitch control with increased effort and reduced margin; degraded law is annunciated.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Function still performed within manoeuvre limits but at significantly reduced capability/margin — a significant reduction, not a loss. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of yaw control authority
rows.effAc: No means of controlling yaw about the vertical axis by any surface; aircraft cannot be held against the sizing directional-control asymmetry (outboard engine out at V1 with maximum blade payload), leading to loss of heading control and departure from controlled flight.
rows.effCrew: Crew unable to arrest yaw/sideslip with available controls; no reversion restores full yaw authority (mechanical reversion reaches the lower rudder segment only).
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only aboard.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of yaw authority against the stated outboard-engine-out directional sizing case precludes continued controlled flight; effects support Catastrophic. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded yaw authority within manoeuvre limits
rows.effAc: Reduced yaw control authority but remaining authority is within the manoeuvre limits required for the flight condition; directional control maintained with reduced margin.
rows.effCrew: Crew retains directional control with a slight reduction in available margin; degradation annunciated (aware case).
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only aboard.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Authority remains within manoeuvre limits with a slight reduction in safety margin and only a slight increase in crew attention; effects support Minor. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded yaw authority outside manoeuvre limits
rows.effAc: Yaw control authority reduced below the manoeuvre limits required for at least one flight condition; directional control margin against the directional-sizing asymmetry is eroded.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only aboard.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is a real reduction below manoeuvre limits, but the SDD gives no residual-authority figure or worst-phase workload for this partial state, so the reduction in safety margin cannot be sized; severity left blank pending residual-authority and crew-workload data.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded yaw authority developing below detection threshold
rows.effAc: Yaw authority degrades progressively while remaining below the annunciation/detection threshold, so the loss of margin accrues without crew awareness.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only aboard.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware condition: classification depends on the detection-threshold magnitude and the residual authority at the point of detection/manifestation, neither of which the SDD provides; abstaining rather than assigning a value.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded yaw divergence below detection threshold
rows.effAc: Uncommanded yaw/sideslip develops slowly below the detection threshold, producing an unannunciated departure from the commanded flight path.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only aboard.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware malfunction: the aircraft effect (and hence severity) depends on the divergence rate versus detection threshold and the state reached before the crew intervenes, which the SDD does not quantify; severity left blank.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement with no crew command
rows.effAc: Uncommanded change in high-lift configuration alters lift and drag with no crew command; at low-altitude, low-speed configuration change points (takeoff/approach/landing) this produces an uncommanded pitch/trim change and a reduction of the speed margin to stall or to structural flap-speed limits.
rows.effCrew: Crew face an unannounced configuration change requiring immediate recognition and manual recovery in a high-workload flight phase.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Large reduction in safety margin (speed/configuration) with excessive crew workload during a low-altitude high-workload phase supports Hazardous. NOTE: the SDD does not quantify the speed-margin loss or resulting handling; confirm against FCS/performance data. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous high-lift response to crew selection
rows.effAc: High-lift configures to a state other than the one selected, so the achieved lift/drag do not match the crew's intended configuration for the phase.
rows.effCrew: Crew act on a configuration they believe is selected while the actual surfaces differ, with recognition dependent on high-lift position indication.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive a class: the SDD states high-lift position is fed to the performance computation but does not quantify the takeoff/landing performance or speed-margin consequence of a mis-configured high-lift on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against ~1,080 m rollout. Missing: performance penalty and control effect of an erroneous configuration. Confirm from FCS/performance data.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment between sides
rows.effAc: Left/right high-lift asymmetry produces an uncommanded rolling moment and lift asymmetry at low speed; asymmetry brakes at each section are intended to arrest a runaway, but a rolling-moment excursion at low altitude reduces roll margin and increases directional/roll control demand.
rows.effCrew: Crew must recognise and counter an asymmetric roll excursion at low speed and low altitude, increasing workload during a critical phase.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded roll asymmetry at low speed/low altitude is a large reduction in safety margin with high crew workload, supporting Hazardous, mitigated by per-section asymmetry brakes. NOTE: the SDD does not quantify the residual roll authority or the excursion the asymmetry brakes permit; confirm against FCS roll-control sizing. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced high-lift configuration range or slower actuation
rows.effAc: High-lift reaches a reduced range or deploys more slowly than commanded, so full takeoff/landing configuration may be unavailable or delayed, affecting achievable lift/drag for the phase.
rows.effCrew: Crew may need to adopt a reduced-flap procedure with associated speed and distance adjustments.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive a class: the SDD does not quantify the takeoff/landing speed increment or landing-distance penalty of a reduced high-lift range against the 1,800 m requirement / ~1,080 m predicted rollout. Missing: performance impact of reduced-flap operation. Confirm from performance data.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of one high-lift device group with remaining available
rows.effAc: One high-lift device group (e.g. one flap section or slat group) is lost while remaining groups function; achievable configuration is reduced and a residual lift/drag or spanwise-load asymmetry may result depending on which group is lost.
rows.effCrew: Crew adopt a reduced-configuration procedure and manage any resulting asymmetry indication.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive a class: the SDD describes four flap sections and full-span slats driven by two PDUs but does not state the aircraft-level effect of losing a single device group — neither the performance penalty nor whether a single-group loss produces a bounded or unbounded asymmetry. Missing: lift/asymmetry and performance consequence of a one-group loss. Confirm from FCS/performance data.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift configuration capability
rows.effAc: Aircraft cannot deploy Fowler flaps or leading-edge slats; takeoff and landing must be flown in a clean or fixed configuration, raising stall and approach speeds and lengthening takeoff and landing distance. Against the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement with ~1,080 m predicted rollout at max landing weight, loss of high-lift materially erodes the operating margin on a surface not maintained to commercial standards.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload managing a high-speed, degraded-configuration approach and landing; diversion to a longer prepared surface likely required.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond the two-to-four flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of high-lift at takeoff/landing produces a large reduction in safety margins and functional capability and excessive crew workload during the most critical phases, on a landing-distance-limited semi-prepared strip. Effects support Hazardous; confirm against the frozen high-lift-out performance case. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous gear position or downlock indication
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify at aircraft level from the provided function definition. The aircraft effect of erroneous indication turns entirely on the crew-awareness split (crew acting on a false 'down-and-locked' versus a false 'unsafe') and on whether the two independent downlock proximity circuits cross-check — neither the resulting aircraft state nor the crew response is stated. Needs the gear-indication logic and the aware/unaware effects before a severity can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded gear movement
rows.effAc: Uncommanded retraction or extension away from the commanded gear state: uncommanded retraction with weight on wheels or during the ground roll would collapse ground support and flotation; uncommanded extension in flight imposes gear loads and drag. Given six three-wheel main bogies and a nose unit sized for semi-prepared flotation, an uncommanded transition of the support function is a loss-of-support event with the aircraft on or near the ground.
rows.effCrew: Startle and high workload; limited or no time to react to an uncommanded ground-phase transition.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects point toward the severe end (uncommanded retraction during ground roll collapses support), but the aircraft-level outcome depends on the gear command architecture and any weight-on-wheels retraction inhibit, which is not stated for gear retraction. Cannot commit a class without the inhibit/interlock design; leaving severity empty rather than guessing.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced footprint flotation on semi-prepared surface
rows.effAc: Reduced ground footprint pressure spreading raises the risk of the gear sinking or the surface failing on the semi-prepared strip, which is not maintained to commercial standards; may cause rutting, gear entrapment or veer during landing rollout and taxi. The tyre and bogie sizing exists specifically to achieve the flotation the semi-prepared surface demands, so a reduction directly attacks the sizing case.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload maintaining directional control on a degrading surface; possible unplanned stop or excursion management.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class: the aircraft consequence of reduced flotation depends on how much footprint is lost and on the gear leg/bogie count, which the SDD states is preliminary and not frozen. Severity ranges from Minor (slight margin reduction, still safely stops) to Hazardous (surface failure, excursion) depending on the degradation magnitude, which is not quantified. Left empty pending the frozen flotation/degraded-footprint case.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of downlock confirmation on one unit
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify at aircraft level. Loss of downlock CONFIRMATION on a single unit is an indication/verification loss, not necessarily a loss of the locked state; the aircraft effect depends on whether the two independent proximity circuits and the free-fall/mechanical downlock still hold the leg locked, and on how a landing is flown with an unconfirmed downlock — none of which is stated at aircraft-function level. Needs the downlock hold/confirm architecture and crew procedure before a severity can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous braking response to pedal command
rows.effAc: Braking output does not match crew pedal command (over- or under-braking), eroding the rollout margin on a semi-prepared surface and risking overrun or loss of directional control.
rows.effCrew: Crew braking inputs produce unexpected deceleration; increased workload to modulate and maintain the runway.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition does not state the magnitude/direction of the error (excess vs deficient braking) or its net ground effect, so the severity-driving outcome cannot be established; anti-skid and dual-supply mitigation not characterised at aircraft level.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Undetected asymmetric braking developing below detection threshold
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware case: the function definition does not state the rate/magnitude the undetected asymmetry develops into, nor the aircraft effect the crew (taking no corrective action) would experience, so no aircraft effect can be stated and severity cannot be derived.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of anti-skid protection with braking retained
rows.effAc: Braking force retained but unmodulated; on the semi-prepared / potentially low-friction destination surface, risk of wheel lock-up, skid and tyre damage, degrading achievable deceleration and directional control during rollout. The friction characteristics of the semi-prepared strip that set the anti-skid benefit are not quantified here.
rows.effCrew: Crew aware via anti-skid status; assumed to modulate braking manually and use reverse thrust.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Anti-skid benefit on the specific semi-prepared surface friction is the driver, and neither the surface friction coefficient nor the resulting rollout penalty is grounded in the provided functions. Cannot map the deceleration loss onto the landing-distance margin, so severity is left blank pending the low-friction-surface rollout analysis.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of one wheel-pair braking
rows.effAc: One wheel pair (of a 20-tyre, six-bogie configuration with per-pair anti-skid) contributes no braking; small reduction in total braking capacity and a possible asymmetric braking tendency requiring directional correction during rollout. The proportional loss from one pair against total capacity is not quantified at this level.
rows.effCrew: Crew aware via braking indication; assumed to correct any asymmetry with steering/pedals and reverse thrust.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The fraction of total braking lost when one of many wheel pairs is out, and the resulting increment on the 1,800 m / 1,080 m margin and on directional control, is not grounded. The gear leg / bogie / tyre count is explicitly preliminary, so the per-pair contribution is not fixed. Cannot classify without that proportion.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded nose-wheel steering deflection
rows.effAc: Uncommanded ground steering deflection produces an unintended lateral/directional excursion during the ground roll; on the semi-prepared strip with ~720 m margin between the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout, a runway/strip lateral excursion or veer-off is credible at speed.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter the uncommanded deflection with differential braking and rudder; significant workload at a high-speed, safety-critical ground phase.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded deflection during high-speed take-off/landing roll on a narrow semi-prepared strip is a large reduction in ground directional-control margins with excessive crew workload to maintain the strip; effects support Hazardous. Awareness/compensation assumed — confirm. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous steering response to crew command
rows.effAc: Steering responds in the wrong sense or magnitude to a crew command, producing a ground track error opposite to or exceeding intent during the roll; risk of lateral excursion on the semi-prepared strip within the ~720 m operating margin.
rows.effCrew: Crew commands one direction and the aircraft responds differently; disorienting mis-response demanding immediate reversion to differential braking/rudder at high workload.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous (wrong-sense) steering response during a high-speed ground roll on a narrow semi-prepared strip is a large reduction in directional-control margins with excessive crew workload; effects support Hazardous. Confirm. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced nose-wheel steering authority
rows.effAc: Reduced steering authority degrades ground directional control; crew retains differential braking and rudder for gross tracking, so strip-keeping is more difficult but achievable at lower speeds.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload to hold the strip centreline using alternative directional means; degraded but manageable ground control.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced (not lost) authority with rudder and differential braking still available is a significant reduction in ground directional-control capability with significant increase in workload; effects support Major. Availability of differential braking assumed — confirm. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose-wheel steering capability
rows.effAc: No nose-wheel steering; ground directional control depends entirely on differential braking and rudder, which lose effectiveness as speed decays. On a narrow semi-prepared strip with the ~720 m margin, maintaining the strip through the roll is significantly degraded.
rows.effCrew: Crew must maintain directional control by differential braking and rudder throughout the roll; significantly increased workload, particularly at low speed where rudder is ineffective.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of steering with differential braking and rudder remaining is a significant reduction in ground directional-control capability and significant workload increase; effects support Major. Whether alternative means preserve strip-keeping on a semi-prepared surface at low speed is an open item — if not, this could rise to Hazardous. Confirm. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded door movement
rows.effAc: Nose visor door moves without command during a ground operation; the door forms part of the pressure boundary and forward fuselage structural load path when closed and comprises the entire nose section. Uncommanded movement during ground handling affects the door/structure and personnel in the loading area.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD states the door 'cannot be operated in flight' and is operated as a ground procedure, so no in-flight aircraft effect is supported by the function definition. The aircraft-level severity of uncommanded door movement on the ground (personnel injury, ground-collision, or structural damage) is not classifiable from the function definition alone — needs the ground-operation hazard scope and crew/ground-personnel exposure to be defined. Severity left empty rather than guessed.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Door fails to reach fully closed position (nose visor not driven to the fully closed position)
rows.effAc: Nose visor not fully closed; aircraft cannot establish the pressure boundary or the forward fuselage structural load path for dispatch. Door is a ground operation and cannot be operated in flight, so the condition is detected on the ground before dispatch.
rows.effCrew: Take-off configuration check flags door not closed/locked; dispatch prevented until resolved.
rows.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight, no passengers carried.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is confined to a ground/dispatch condition detected before flight; the SDD does not state an aircraft-level in-flight effect for a door that fails to close, and states the door cannot be operated in flight. Cannot derive an in-flight severity without a stated dispatch-availability / turnaround effect. Confirm whether a no-dispatch condition carries any classified aircraft effect.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of primary door drive with backup drive available
rows.effAc: Primary hydraulic door drive lost; door still opened/closed via the electric backup drive. Full door open/close capability retained by an alternate means.
rows.effCrew: Reduced door-drive redundancy; may require alternate-drive procedure during ground operation.
rows.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Backup drive preserves full door open/close capability during a ground operation; the SDD does not state an aircraft-level effect for loss of one door drive with the alternate available, and the door is not operated in flight. Cannot derive a severity without a stated dispatch/turnaround availability effect.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose door open/close capability
rows.effAc: Door cannot be opened or closed by any means. If unable to close: no dispatch (no pressure boundary, no structural load path). If unable to open: cannot load/unload the blade at the destination strip. Door is a ground operation and cannot be operated in flight.
rows.effCrew: Loading/unloading operation blocked; dispatch or mission-completion prevented on the ground.
rows.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Complete loss manifests as a ground dispatch/mission-availability condition detected before flight; the SDD states the door cannot be operated in flight and does not assign an aircraft-level in-flight effect to loss of open/close capability. Cannot derive an in-flight severity without a stated availability effect. Note the closed-and-locked case is covered by SF-011.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous confirmation of a lock state not achieved (indication reports the nose door locked/secured when the locking pins are not fully engaged)
rows.effAc: Nose visor indicated locked but not fully secured; the forward pressure boundary and forward fuselage structural load path are not established as believed. With the take-off configuration check satisfied by the erroneous indication, the aircraft can be dispatched with an unlatched primary structural / pressure-boundary door, leading to loss of pressure-boundary integrity and potential in-flight door failure / structural release.
rows.effCrew: Crew have no true annunciation of the unlocked state and continue normally; both lock-sensing paths would have to be defeated to produce this condition.
rows.effPax: None carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected unlatched nose visor — a primary structural and pressure-boundary element forming the forward fuselage load path — can lead to in-flight door departure / loss of structural integrity and loss of the airplane. Proposed for confirmation; the SDD describes the design but classifies nothing, and dual dissimilar sensing bears on the likelihood, not the severity. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous unlock permission with hold pressurised (lock actuator permitted to run / pressure interlock defeated while a pressure differential exists)
rows.effAc: Pressure interlock that should inhibit unlock until residual differential is below 0.1 psi is defeated; unlock is permitted with the hold pressurised. If unlatching proceeds under differential the nose visor can be released under pressure load, causing rapid depressurisation and loss of the primary structural / pressure-boundary door in flight.
rows.effCrew: Crew reliant on the interlock; if defeated, an unlock command or actuator run under pressure is not prevented as designed.
rows.effPax: None carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the pressure interlock permitting unlatch of the nose visor under differential can release a primary structural / pressure-boundary door in flight, leading to loss of the airplane. Proposed for confirmation; contingent on the door being operable/unlockable in flight and on the preliminary hold differential — the SDD states the door cannot be operated in flight, so confirm whether an in-flight unlock path exists to support this classification. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous confirmation that the nose door is lock-secure while it is not fully locked (crew unaware, continue normal duties)
rows.effAc: Take-off configuration monitor is satisfied by the erroneous confirmation and the aircraft is dispatched with the nose visor not fully locked; the visor forms the pressure boundary and part of the forward-fuselage load path, so an in-flight loss of visor retention is a potential loss of the pressure boundary and structural load path.
rows.effCrew: Crew receive a valid lock-secure indication and take no corrective action; no annunciation of the true unlocked state.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected directly.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous confirmation defeats the only barrier (the take-off configuration check) against dispatch with an unlocked visor; in-flight failure of a pressure-boundary and forward-fuselage load-path element is a potential loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced locking redundancy or single lock-sensing path lost, remaining locking and confirmation available
rows.effAc: Locking and its confirmation are still performed by the remaining latches/pins and remaining sensing path; the closed-door pressure boundary and load path remain established.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected directly.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — With residual locking and confirmation the function is still performed; the SDD function definition does not establish whether the degraded state is dispatched, drives a crew-workload or safety-margin effect, or is a ground-only maintenance finding — the aircraft-level effect cannot be grounded, so severity is left blank.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of one of the two dissimilar, independently routed lock-sensing paths; the other sensing path remains
rows.effAc: Lock state is still confirmed by the remaining dissimilar sensing path (proximity harness or mechanical visual indicator); locking itself is unaffected and the pressure boundary/load path remain established.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected directly.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Dual dissimilar independently routed sensing means the remaining path still confirms lock state; the function definition does not establish whether loss of one path is dispatchable or produces a crew-workload/margin effect, so the aircraft-level effect cannot be grounded and severity is left blank.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of door-closure locking and confirmation capability
rows.effAc: No means to lock the nose visor and no means to confirm a lock state; the door is a ground-operated item and cannot be operated in flight, so the condition is a ground/dispatch state governing whether the aircraft is released with an unlocked or unconfirmed visor.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected directly.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft-level effect turns on whether complete loss of locking/confirmation results in a detected no-dispatch (no aircraft effect) versus dispatch with an unlocked visor (potential loss of the airplane); the door being ground-operated only, and the dispatch outcome, are not established by the function definition, so severity cannot be derived and is left blank.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Restraint mechanically locked and confirming secure but not carrying rated load (crew unaware, continue normal duties)
rows.effAc: A single blade of up to 72.6 t is effectively unrestrained longitudinally while indication shows secure; under flight or ground load cases the payload can shift, producing a large centre-of-gravity excursion and structural loading beyond design intent — a potential loss of the airplane.
rows.effCrew: Crew receive a valid restraint-secure indication and take no corrective action; no in-flight adjustment of restraint is available.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected directly.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An erroneously secure indication with a 72.6 t single unitised payload not actually restrained gives no barrier against an uncommanded longitudinal shift in flight; the resulting CG excursion and structural overload are a potential loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of longitudinal payload restraint — the single blade is unrestrained longitudinally
rows.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
rows.effAc: Unrestrained 72.6 t blade free to translate longitudinally along the 108 m hold under flight/ground load cases; large uncommanded shift of centre of gravity outside limits and gross load redistribution on the hold floor structure; controllability and structural integrity threatened.
rows.effCrew: Crew has in-flight indication only and no means of in-flight restraint adjustment; abrupt CG excursion may exceed recoverable control.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant exposure, but loss of aircraft control endangers flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A single 72.6 t blade translating uncommanded drives CG outside limits with no in-flight recovery means; effects support loss of the airplane. Proposed for engineer confirmation. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced longitudinal restraint capacity at one or more stations
rows.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
rows.effAc: Restraint retained but at reduced capacity at one or more of the nine stations; per the design, loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, so a limited reduction may remain within the restrained-load path with reduced margin to a full-restraint failure.
rows.effCrew: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight; loss on two adjacent stations is annunciated as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention. Crew has indication only, no in-flight adjustment.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant exposure.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on how many stations are degraded and whether the remaining load paths hold the 72.6 t blade within limits for the applicable phase; the model gives the redundancy claim (neighbour carries one lost strap) but not the number of stations degraded nor the resulting reduction in safety margin, so the effect cannot be pinned to one class. Left blank pending the degradation extent and structural margin data.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced restraint tension below required at one or more stations
rows.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
rows.effAc: Straps present but tension below required at one or more stations; longitudinal restraint margin reduced, with potential for small blade movement or increased load transfer to remaining stations, degrading margin to a restraint failure.
rows.effCrew: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight; two adjacent stations annunciated as requiring immediate attention. Crew has indication only.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant exposure.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft effect of a below-required tension depends on how far below required and at how many stations, and whether the blade can move within limits — the model states the monitoring and annunciation but not the tolerance band, number of stations, or resulting margin loss. Cannot derive a class; left blank.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Restraint mechanically locked but not carrying rated tension — restraint status reads engaged while load is not carried
rows.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
rows.effAc: Straps mechanically locked but not carrying rated load, so the blade is effectively unrestrained to the extent of the shortfall while the restraint appears engaged; potential for uncommanded blade movement and CG excursion equivalent toward the complete-loss case, with reduced or no warning to the crew.
rows.effCrew: Restraint appears secure; the single instrumented tension monitoring loop is the only coverage and its coverage is a recorded item, so a locked-but-unloaded condition may not be reliably annunciated — misleading status.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant exposure, but crew acts on misleading restraint status.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The worst outcome trends toward the unrestrained (Catastrophic candidate) case, but the class turns on whether the single tension monitoring loop detects a locked-but-unloaded strap and on how much rated load is not carried; the model states the loop is single and its coverage is a recorded item but does not establish detection of this specific condition. Cannot commit a class without that detectability determination; left blank.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced available forward thrust (below commanded/required, all remaining thrust symmetric)
rows.effAc: Reduced climb and acceleration capability and reduced performance margins; the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following loss of any one engine at or after V1, but a general symmetric thrust shortfall reduces performance margins without necessarily being controllable-flight-limiting.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload managing a performance shortfall; possible need to select a nearer aerodrome or amend the flight profile.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects as stated support a significant reduction in performance margins (MAJ-1) for a partial symmetric loss. Suggested, not committed: the aircraft-level magnitude of the shortfall is not quantified in the SDD; a shortfall approaching total loss would drive higher — confirm the loss band and worst phase (takeoff). [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of pitch control authority
rows.effAc: Aircraft cannot be trimmed or manoeuvred in pitch by any means; loss of longitudinal control of trajectory. With mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim only, controllability is not assured across the envelope.
rows.effCrew: Crew unable to arrest pitch excursion or maintain flightpath; no effective compensating action available for total loss.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of pitch control of trajectory is a loss-of-airplane condition; effects support CAT-1. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded pitch authority outside manoeuvre limits
rows.effAc: Pitch authority reduced below that required for the manoeuvre envelope; aircraft cannot achieve required longitudinal manoeuvre in one or more phases, large reduction in safety margins.
rows.effCrew: Crew faces significantly increased workload flying a degraded law with reduced authority; manoeuvre restrictions required.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Authority below the required manoeuvre envelope is a large reduction in functional capability; effects support HAZ-1. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded pitch authority developing below detection threshold
rows.effAc: Pitch authority erodes slowly below the crew-detection threshold; on demand the aircraft cannot meet the required manoeuvre, encountered without warning, a large reduction in safety margins.
rows.effCrew: Crew unaware, continue normal duties and take no action; degradation revealed only when authority is demanded, reducing time to react.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected latent loss of manoeuvre authority, discovered on demand, is a large reduction in safety margins; effects support HAZ-1. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response to crew command
rows.effAc: Yaw surface responds erroneously to crew input; aircraft develops directional excursion not matching intent, with sideslip/bank coupling. Given the outboard-engine-out directional sizing case, margins against loss of directional control can be significantly reduced.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter the erroneous response, materially increased workload; effectiveness depends on phase and available authority.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous directional response producing an uncommanded excursion is a large reduction in safety margins; effects support HAZ-1. Phase sensitivity noted — near-ground excursion may warrant re-examination. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw motion with no crew command
rows.effAc: Yaw develops with no crew command; uncommanded directional excursion with sideslip and roll coupling. Against the directional sizing basis this is a large reduction in safety margins.
rows.effCrew: Crew must recognise an unexpected uncommanded yaw and arrest it, materially increased workload; effectiveness depends on phase and residual authority.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded directional excursion is a large reduction in safety margins; effects support HAZ-1. Phase dependence flagged — a near-ground uncommanded yaw may drive a worse classification and should be re-examined. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground support / flotation capability
rows.effAc: Aircraft loses ground support/flotation on a semi-prepared surface; gear or flotation collapse on touchdown or rollout leads to structural collapse and departure from the prepared strip.
rows.effCrew: Crew unable to arrest or control the aircraft on the ground; excessive workload with no effective recovery.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: On a semi-prepared strip at max landing weight the loss of ground support/flotation at touchdown/rollout is potential loss of the airplane; effects support CAT-1. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded braking with no crew command
rows.effAc: Uncommanded braking at speed on the ground erodes the take-off/rollout margin (1,800 m required vs ~1,080 m predicted), risking directional excursion, tyre/brake overload or overrun off the semi-prepared strip.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter an uncommanded deceleration; increased workload to maintain directional control.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded braking at speed produces a large reduction in ground safety margins/directional control on a short semi-prepared strip; effects support HAZ-1. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric braking between left and right
rows.effAc: Left/right brake asymmetry induces a yawing moment during high-speed ground roll, driving the aircraft off the centreline of a semi-prepared strip with limited margin to counter.
rows.effCrew: Crew must apply corrective steering/rudder to hold the centreline; high workload during the deceleration.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetric braking at speed on a short semi-prepared strip is a large reduction in directional-control safety margins with a lateral excursion risk; effects support HAZ-1. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced wheel braking effectiveness (crew aware)
rows.effAc: Reduced deceleration on landing rollout; the SDD margin between the 1,800 m landing requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout is partially consumed. Exact remaining stopping distance depends on the amount of degradation, which is not quantified at aircraft-function level here.
rows.effCrew: Crew aware via brake system indication; assumed to apply reverse thrust (inboard reversers) and manage rollout within the available margin.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect scales with the DEGREE of degradation, which the function definition does not quantify. Without the fraction of braking lost mapped against the 1,800 m / 1,080 m margin, the crossing point between MIN-1 (slight reduction in safety margins) and MAJ-1 (significant reduction) cannot be grounded. Need the degraded-braking rollout figure to classify.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Undetected reduced braking effectiveness (crew unaware)
rows.effAc: Braking effectiveness reduced but not annunciated; crew continue normal duties and apply braking expecting nominal deceleration. Deceleration is lower than planned and the operating margin between the 1,800 m landing requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout is consumed silently, with runway overrun on the semi-prepared strip a credible outcome where the degradation is large.
rows.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no corrective action regarding the degradation; late recognition through decelerometer feel gives little rollout distance to react on a strip with no line maintenance and limited overrun.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected degradation with the crew acting normally can consume the landing-distance margin on a semi-prepared strip and produce a runway overrun — a large reduction in safety margins with the crew unable to compensate because they are unaware. Proposed Hazardous per HAZ-1; confirm against the degraded-rollout distance and the overrun consequence on the destination surface. If large degradation is shown non-survivable, revisit toward Catastrophic. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel braking capability
rows.effAc: No wheel braking from any source (normal system B, alternate system A, and accumulator reserve exhausted). On landing the aircraft cannot decelerate by wheel braking; only inboard reverse thrust and aerodynamic drag remain. Against the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m nominal rollout with braking, the residual deceleration is insufficient and runway overrun on the semi-prepared strip is a credible outcome; a rejected take-off with no braking is more severe still.
rows.effCrew: Crew aware via braking indication; assumed to deploy inboard reverse thrust and use all available drag, but with no wheel braking the crew cannot arrest the aircraft within the available surface.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of wheel braking with only two inboard reversers and aerodynamic drag remaining, against a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip and no overrun provision, credibly leads to a high-energy overrun / loss of the airplane, particularly on a rejected take-off. Proposed Catastrophic per CAT-1; confirm against the no-braking stopping distance with reverse-thrust-only and the strip end condition. Note the six-application accumulator reserve means fully-total loss requires that reserve also depleted. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous forward thrust not matching commanded setting (thrust differs from thrust-lever demand)
rows.effAc: Aircraft trajectory/energy does not match the commanded state; if symmetric across engines, primarily an energy-management error rather than a directional one.
rows.effCrew: Crew must detect the discrepancy between commanded and delivered thrust and reconfigure; workload increase.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The provided material does not establish the magnitude, direction (over/under), symmetry, or crew annunciation of the erroneous thrust, so the resulting aircraft effect cannot be bounded (an undetected symmetric under-thrust on take-off differs sharply from a minor cruise error). Severity left blank pending definition of the erroneous-thrust characteristics and the alerting available.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced available forward thrust (below commanded/required, symmetric)
rows.effAc: Reduced climb/acceleration capability; the SDD states the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine at or after V1, so a bounded thrust reduction is within the dispatch design case, but a larger deficit reduces performance margins.
rows.effCrew: Crew manages degraded performance, may require diversion/level-off; workload increase.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8).
