SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The condition spans from a single-engine-equivalent loss (explicitly within the continue-to-aerodrome design case) to a larger multi-engine deficit (loss of a second engine on the same side is stated as outside the design dispatch case and retained for study). A ground-turnaround inconvenience at a strip with no line maintenance may be operationally significant but the SF-010 function definition does not state an aircraft-level safety effect; left empty rather than defaulting to No Safety Effect.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose door open/close capability (total loss of open/close function)
rows.effAc: Door cannot be opened or closed by any means on the ground. If stuck closed and locked: cannot load/unload but pressure boundary and structural load path intact — no in-flight airworthiness effect. If stuck open: aircraft cannot be dispatched. Door cannot be operated in flight, so no in-flight failure.
rows.effCrew: Loading/unloading prevented; dispatch decision taken at origin considering outbound and return together, with no line maintenance at the strip.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no passenger effect.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — A total loss of open/close capability is a ground/dispatch and mission-availability condition; the door cannot be operated in flight and (if closed and locked) the pressure boundary and load path are unaffected. The SF-010 function definition does not state an in-flight aircraft effect, so an aircraft-level severity cannot be derived — left empty. The safety-driving conditions are the lock/confirmation malfunctions under SF-011.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous lock-secure confirmation of the nose cargo door with the door not fully locked
rows.effAc: Crew accept a lock-secure indication and dispatch/pressurise with the nose visor — a pressure-boundary and forward structural load-path element (SDD §5.7.1) — not fully locked; latches may back-drive under load with pins not engaged, risking in-flight loss of the door and depressurisation of the hold.
rows.effCrew: Crew unaware of the true unlocked state; no corrective action taken because indication is misleading.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed in the hold.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Misleading confirmation defeats the take-off configuration check and both dissimilar sensing paths' purpose; in-flight loss of a nose visor forming the pressure boundary and forward structural load path can lead to loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced locking redundancy or single lock-sensing path lost on the nose cargo door
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed in the hold.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD establishes dual dissimilar sensing and twelve latches / eight pins on two supplies, but does not state the aircraft-level effect of dispatching or continuing with reduced locking redundancy or a single sensing path lost; the surviving path still confirms lock. No aircraft effect is grounded, so severity is left empty pending the dispatch/continued-operation policy for reduced redundancy.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of one of two dissimilar nose-door lock-sensing paths
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed in the hold.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Dual dissimilar sensing (proximity harness plus mechanical linkage/indicator) means the surviving path still confirms lock state; the SDD does not state the aircraft-level effect of operating with one sensing path lost, so no effect can be grounded and severity is left empty.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose door-closure locking and confirmation
rows.effAc: No means to lock the visor or confirm its lock state; the door, forming the pressure boundary and forward fuselage structural load path when closed (SDD §5.7.1), cannot be assured secured. Pressurising or flying with an unassured lock risks in-flight loss of the door and depressurisation. Note the pressure interlock inhibits unlock while pressurised (SDD §5.7.2), which mitigates inadvertent unlocking but not loss of positive locking.
rows.effCrew: Crew have no valid lock confirmation; dispatch would be precluded by absence of the configuration-check indication.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed in the hold.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of positive locking and its confirmation on a door that is the pressure boundary and forward structural load path can, if flown, lead to in-flight door loss and loss of the airplane; the configuration-check dependency and pressure interlock mitigate but do not eliminate the load-path/pressure hazard. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous restraint locking indicated but not carrying rated load
rows.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Landing
rows.effAc: Restraint indicates locked/secure but a strap set does not carry rated longitudinal load; under flight or ground load cases the single 72.6 t blade may shift longitudinally, driving centre-of-gravity outside limits and imposing loads the structure and control were not sized for. Blade shift on a 105 m unitised payload is a loss-of-control / structural-overload hazard.
rows.effCrew: Crew rely on a false secure indication; tension monitoring loop may not reveal a locked-but-unloaded strap, so no corrective action is taken.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed in the hold.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A single 72.6 t blade occupying the full hold length shifting longitudinally in flight produces uncontrollable CG excursion and structural overload; effects support loss of the airplane. Confirm against the restraint substantiation and whether the tension loop detects a locked-but-unloaded strap. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: complete loss of longitudinal payload restraint
rows.effAc: The single unitised blade (up to 72.6 t occupying the full hold length) is unrestrained longitudinally; any acceleration or attitude change permits the mass to translate along the hold, producing a large uncontrolled centre-of-gravity shift and impact loads on hold structure not designed to react a moving payload.
rows.effCrew: Crew has in-flight indication only with no means of re-restraining the payload; an uncontrollable CG excursion is beyond crew recovery.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant injury, but loss of aircraft control endangers the flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncontrolled longitudinal shift of a 72.6 t unitised mass drives a CG excursion beyond controllable limits and structural overload — loss of the airplane. Proposed for your confirmation. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: restraint mechanically locked but not carrying rated tension
rows.effAc: Restraint presents as engaged but does not carry rated load; under flight or ground load cases the affected station(s) allow the blade to move, producing an unannounced longitudinal shift of the unitised mass and a progressive centre-of-gravity excursion.
rows.effCrew: Crew is unaware — indication shows locked/engaged while rated tension is absent; crew continues normally and takes no action, so the latent condition is revealed only by an eventual uncommanded payload movement.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant injury, but an undetected loss of effective restraint endangers the flight crew through loss of control.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Unaware condition on a 72.6 t unitised payload: effective restraint is absent while indicated present, so it can propagate to the same uncontrolled CG excursion as total loss. Proposed for your confirmation; note the erroneous-confirmation aspect (indication reads locked while tension not carried) is a monitoring-integrity claim to be substantiated. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: reduced longitudinal restraint capacity at one or more stations
rows.effAc: Restraint capacity is reduced at one or more stations; the SDD states neighbouring straps carry a lost strap and that single-strap loss is annunciated, but the residual restraint margin and the resulting aircraft effect are not quantified.
rows.effCrew: Loss of a strap is annunciated in flight; loss on two adjacent stations is annunciated as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention — the crew response and its result are not defined in the provided material.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant injury stated.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded from the SDD: the document annunciates degraded restraint and asserts neighbours carry a lost strap, but gives no quantified residual load-path margin, so the aircraft effect of the degradation cannot be stated. A restraint load-path / margin analysis is needed before a class can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: reduced restraint tension below required at one or more stations
rows.effAc: Strap tension at one or more stations falls below the required value; the amount of slack, the resulting permissible payload movement and the aircraft effect are not quantified in the provided material.
rows.effCrew: Tension loss on any strap is annunciated in flight; adjacent-station loss is annunciated as requiring immediate attention — no in-flight adjustment is available, and the assumed crew action and its result are not defined.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant injury stated.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded from the SDD: the provided material annunciates below-tension conditions but does not quantify the permitted payload movement or the resulting margin, so the aircraft effect and hence the class cannot be derived. Requires restraint tension-margin / load-path analysis.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric forward thrust across the aircraft (uncommanded thrust split between sides)
rows.effAc: Yawing/rolling moment toward the low-thrust side; worst case approximates the outboard-engine directional-control sizing case at the 28 m moment arm. Requires substantial rudder to hold heading; safety margins reduced.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload to detect the asymmetry, identify the affected engine(s), and apply directional correction; higher during take-off/initial climb.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded thrust asymmetry approaching the outboard-engine sizing case produces a large reduction in safety margins and directional-control difficulty, with elevated crew workload; effects support Hazardous per HAZ-1. Not proposed Catastrophic as the SDD carries directional authority sized for the outboard-engine case; engineer to confirm against the actual asymmetry magnitude range. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of forward thrust generation (all four engines)
rows.effAc: Total loss of propulsive thrust; aircraft cannot sustain flight and is committed to a forced descent/landing off the available energy state.
rows.effCrew: Crew flies a power-off descent/forced landing; extreme workload with no propulsive recovery available.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed; loss of the airplane implicates flight crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of all forward thrust denies sustained flight and results in loss of the airplane; effects support Catastrophic per CAT-1. Independence of the total-loss (common-cause across all four engines) is not the FHA's concern — the effect drives the class. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Uncommanded reverse thrust deployment
rows.effAc: In flight, an uncommanded reverser deployment (inboard engine) produces a large asymmetric drag/thrust moment and control disturbance; the SDD provides in-flight inhibition (weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter agreement) and a mechanical translating-sleeve lock, so an in-flight deployment is a defeat of those interlocks. On the ground, an uncommanded deployment affects directional control during the roll.
rows.effCrew: Crew must counter the asymmetric moment and identify/secure the affected engine; high workload, more severe if in flight.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded in-flight reverse-thrust deployment on an inboard engine produces a large asymmetric moment and reduction in controllability/safety margins, supporting Hazardous per HAZ-1. Proposed, not committed: whether the effect reaches Catastrophic depends on the phase (low-speed take-off/initial climb) and the residual controllability with the disturbance, which the provided material does not quantify; engineer to confirm the worst-phase controllability. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground reverse thrust (both inboard reversers unavailable) during the landing roll
rows.effAc: Loss of the reverse-thrust deceleration contribution on the ground; stopping relies wholly on wheel braking and aerodynamic drag. On the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against a predicted ~1,080 m rollout the retardation margin is reduced; on a contaminated or reduced-friction surface stopping distance may increase toward the available length.
rows.effCrew: Increased crew workload to manage deceleration by braking alone; possible need for maximum braking and early crew attention.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Reverse thrust augments deceleration but wheel braking is the primary ground-stopping means (SDD: predicted rollout ~1,080 m vs 1,800 m requirement, that margin is the basis on which braking/reverse degradation is assessed). Whether loss of reverse alone produces a 'significant reduction in safety margins' (MAJ-1) or only a slight one (MIN-1) depends on the achievable stopping distance without reverse on the semi-prepared / contaminated surface — landing-distance-without-reverse performance data is not in the SDD, so the class cannot be derived here.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced ground reverse thrust (partial loss, e.g. one inboard reverser unavailable or reduced authority) during the landing roll
rows.effAc: Reduced reverse-thrust deceleration contribution; wheel braking remains the primary stopping means. Small increase in stopping distance relative to full reverse; a single-reverser case also introduces a residual directional asymmetry that anti-skid steering must accommodate.
rows.effCrew: Slight increase in crew workload to compensate with braking and, for a single-reverser case, directional correction.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is a reduction in deceleration augmentation with wheel braking retained. Whether the residual stopping-distance and asymmetry effect is a slight reduction in margin (MIN-1) or more depends on the achievable-distance and directional data not stated in the SDD; class left blank rather than guessed.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on the ground (one inboard reverser deploying/producing reverse while the other does not, crew aware)
rows.effAc: Yawing moment toward the higher-reverse side during the ground roll on a semi-prepared, potentially low-friction surface; risk of directional deviation / runway excursion if not corrected. Nose-wheel steering and differential braking are the available directional means.
rows.effCrew: Crew aware via alerting and aircraft response; assumed to reduce/cancel reverse and apply directional correction (steering, differential braking). Elevated workload during a time-critical ground manoeuvre.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The effect is a directional-control excursion hazard on a narrow-margin semi-prepared strip, which could support MAJ-1 or higher, but the outcome depends on the correctable asymmetric moment vs available steering/braking authority and runway width — directional-control-on-ground margin data is not in the SDD. Class not derivable; left blank.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust developing on the ground below the detection threshold (crew unaware, no corrective action taken)
rows.effAc: An asymmetric yawing moment builds during the ground roll without annunciation; with the crew continuing normally and taking no corrective action, directional deviation accumulates unopposed toward a possible runway excursion on the semi-prepared strip.
rows.effCrew: Crew unaware and take no action regarding the condition; directional correction is delayed until aircraft response becomes apparent, by which point deviation may be established.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — With no annunciation and no crew action assumed, an undetected asymmetric ground moment is potentially more severe than the aware case (SF-002-M2), tending toward a directional-control / excursion condition. Whether it reaches HAZ-1 or CAT-1 depends on the magnitude of the undetected moment, how far deviation develops before it becomes apparent, and runway width — none of which is quantified in the SDD. Class left blank per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command (roll surfaces respond incorrectly to, or opposite/disproportionate to, the commanded roll)
rows.effAc: Aircraft rolls in an unintended sense or magnitude relative to the crew's command; potential departure from the intended flight path and, if uncorrected, loss of control, particularly at low altitude (take-off / approach / landing) or during the engine-out blade-loaded directional-control sizing case.
rows.effCrew: Crew must recognise the erroneous response and counter it; if the roll opposes or exceeds the intended command the situation may be difficult to diagnose and correct within the available time and altitude.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An erroneous roll response that the crew cannot arrest can result in departure from controlled flight and loss of the airplane, especially at low altitude — the stated effect supports the CAT-1 anchor (loss of the airplane). Proposed for engineer confirmation; a controllability/handling analysis and the roll-authority margins would confirm whether recovery is assured in every phase. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Degraded pitch authority outside manoeuvre limits
rows.effAc: Pitch authority insufficient to command the manoeuvres required in the operating envelope; large reduction in safety margins with potential inability to maintain the flight path in critical phases.
rows.effCrew: Crew commands cannot achieve required pitch response; excessive workload without recovery in the limiting phases.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of pitch authority BELOW that needed for required manoeuvres (outside manoeuvre limits) removes the ability to maintain the flight path in the limiting take-off/landing phases; effects support loss of the airplane. If review judges residual authority still permits a survivable degraded flight-path, this reduces to Hazardous (HAZ-1) — engineer to confirm against the pitch sizing case. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response to crew command
rows.effAc: Yaw axis responds differently from the commanded input; misleading/erroneous directional response can drive the aircraft toward loss of directional control, most critically at the outboard-engine-out condition the rudder is sized for.
rows.effCrew: Crew directional inputs produce the wrong response; recovery may be impossible in the directional-control limiting case.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Yaw is a primary trajectory axis (SF-005 implements 'Control aircraft trajectory'). An erroneous yaw response at or near the sizing case — outboard engine failure at the 28 m moment arm with maximum blade payload — threatens loss of directional control and loss of the airplane. Magnitude of the erroneous response is undefined by the function statement; if bounded to a recoverable transient, reassess (potentially HAZ-1). [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous gear position or downlock indication (indication does not reflect the true gear/downlock state)
rows.effAc: Crew may believe the gear is down and locked when it is not, risking landing with a leg unlocked or retracted; or believe a leg is unlocked when it is down, prompting an unnecessary go-around/free-fall. Landing on an unlocked or collapsed leg on a semi-prepared strip risks gear collapse and loss of ground controllability.
rows.effCrew: Misleading indication drives an incorrect gear-configuration decision; increased workload cross-checking dual sensing and considering alternate extension.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Misleading downlock indication can lead to landing with a gear leg not locked, a large reduction in safety margins on a semi-prepared strip; classified against HAZ-1. Proposed for engineer confirmation; note dual dissimilar downlock sensing per unit is a mitigating architectural feature to weigh. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced wheel braking effectiveness
rows.effAc: Braking effort reduced; landing rollout increases against the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement, eroding the margin over the ~1,080 m predicted rollout. On the short strip with no line maintenance a reduced-braking landing narrows or consumes the stopping margin.
rows.effCrew: Increased workload managing a longer stop; may need to apply reverse thrust (inboard engines) and maximum braking; possible go-around/diversion decision.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects place this between MAJ-1 (significant reduction in landing safety margin/functional capability) and HAZ-1 depending on how much of the 1,800 m vs 1,080 m margin is consumed and the reverser-thrust/diversion mitigation available; the SDD gives the margin but not the braking-effectiveness reduction magnitude that would decide the class. Left empty pending the degradation quantum and residual-margin analysis.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of anti-skid protection with braking retained
rows.effAc: Braking retained but without per-wheel-pair anti-skid modulation; on a semi-prepared (low/variable friction) surface, wheel lock and skid degrade achievable deceleration and directional stability, increasing rollout and risk of tyre burst on 20 tyres.
rows.effCrew: Crew must modulate brake pedals manually to avoid lockup; increased workload and attention during rollout on a marginal surface.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Anti-skid loss on a variable-friction semi-prepared surface plausibly reduces the landing safety margin (MAJ-1) and raises crew workload (MAJ-2), but the achievable deceleration without anti-skid on this surface, and whether it still meets the 1,800 m requirement, is not stated in the SDD. Left empty pending the no-anti-skid stopping-performance analysis.. Engineer to classify.

rows.fcDesc: Loss of one wheel-pair braking
rows.effAc: One wheel pair unbraked of twenty tyres across six main bogies; small reduction in total braking force and a small asymmetric braking moment during rollout, correctable within remaining braking and steering.
rows.effCrew: Slight increase in workload to correct minor asymmetry and account for marginally longer stop.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond crew.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of braking on one wheel pair out of twenty tyres (six three-wheel main bogies) is a small fraction of total braking capability with anti-skid on remaining pairs; effects are a slight reduction in stopping margin and slight crew workload increase to correct minor asymmetry — MIN-1 / MIN-2. Proposed for confirmation. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel braking capability
rows.effAc: No wheel braking from normal (system B), alternate (system A) or accumulator reserve; deceleration on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip depends only on aerodynamic drag and inboard reverse thrust, with the predicted ~1,080 m rollout margin lost and a high likelihood of runway excursion/overrun off the end of an unprepared surface.
rows.effCrew: Maximum reverse thrust and any residual retardation applied; no braking or steering-via-differential-braking authority; excessive workload and a probable overrun the crew cannot arrest.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond crew, though an overrun risks airframe damage/loss.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of wheel braking on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip removes the primary means of decelerating within the available length; residual retardation is reverse thrust (inboard engines only) plus aerodynamic drag. Proposed HAZ-1 (large reduction in functional capability / safety margin, excessive crew workload). Whether the residual outcome is a survivable overrun (Hazardous) or loss of the airplane (Catastrophic, CAT-1) depends on overrun terrain and reverser-thrust stopping analysis not in the SDD — confirm the class. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Reduced nose-wheel steering authority
rows.effAc: Steering authority is reduced but present; directional control on the ground is still available through remaining steering plus differential braking and rudder, at reduced precision. Manoeuvring on the semi-prepared strip is degraded.
rows.effCrew: Crew maintains directional control using differential braking and rudder in addition to reduced steering; increased workload, particularly for the tight-turnaround ground manoeuvring at the destination strip.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Directional control on the ground remains available by the alternate means the SDD describes (differential braking and rudder pedals), with reduced steering authority producing a slight increase in crew workload and slightly reduced ground manoeuvring precision — consistent with MIN-2. If ground handling analysis shows the residual authority is inadequate on the semi-prepared strip this must be reconsidered. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose-wheel steering capability
rows.effAc: No nose-wheel steering; directional control on the ground is by differential braking and rudder only. The aircraft can be kept on the prepared surface at speed by rudder and differential braking, but low-speed manoeuvring and tight turnaround handling on the semi-prepared strip are substantially degraded.
rows.effCrew: Crew controls direction by differential braking and rudder throughout the ground roll and taxi; significantly increased workload, particularly for manoeuvring on the constrained destination strip.
rows.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of primary ground directional-control means with an available alternate (differential braking and rudder) represents a significant reduction in ground manoeuvring capability and a significant increase in crew workload — consistent with MAJ-1/MAJ-2. Whether the alternate is adequate on the semi-prepared strip should be substantiated by ground-handling analysis; if it is not, escalation is warranted. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous confirmation of a lock state that was not actually achieved (misleading lock indication)
rows.effAc: Flight deck and take-off configuration monitor indicate the visor locked when latches/pins are not fully engaged. The visor forms the forward pressure boundary and part of the forward fuselage structural load path when closed; an undetected unlocked/mis-latched visor risks in-flight loss of the pressure boundary and of a primary structural load path. Design mitigation is dual dissimilar, independently routed lock sensing (proximity harness + mechanical visual indicator).
rows.effCrew: Crew are misled into believing the door is secure and take no corrective action; the erroneous confirmation defeats the take-off configuration check.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no direct passenger injury path, but loss of forward pressure boundary / structural load path threatens the airframe.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An erroneous 'locked' confirmation removes the crew's and the configuration monitor's defence against an unsecured visor which is both the forward pressure boundary and part of the forward fuselage structural load path; undetected in-flight failure of that load path/boundary is a potential loss of the airplane. Proposed as a candidate CAT-1 for engineer confirmation, credited against the dual dissimilar independent lock sensing whose independence must be verified (see assumptions). [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

rows.fcDesc: Erroneous unlock permission granted with the hold pressurised (unlock interlock defeated in flight)
rows.effAc: The unlock/lock actuator is permitted to run against a pressurised hold, defeating the pressure interlock that should vent and confirm residual differential below 0.1 psi before unlock. Driving the pins/latches with the hold pressurised risks rapid loss of the forward pressure boundary and release of a primary forward-fuselage structural load path in flight.
rows.effCrew: No timely crew defence if the interlock is bypassed; the door is not intended to be operable in flight and the crew would not expect an unlock to be possible.
rows.effPax: No occupants in the hold; the hazard is loss of pressure boundary / structural load path and potential loss of the airplane.
rows.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Defeating the pressure interlock so unlock proceeds against a pressurised hold in flight can release the forward pressure boundary and a primary structural load path — a potential loss of the airplane, so proposed as candidate CAT-1 for engineer confirmation. Credit for the pressure interlock (vents and confirms < 0.1 psi before the actuator runs) and for the door being non-operable in flight must be verified before any lower class is accepted. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.
